Now, to build a Viksit Bharat, we need a new current. Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the 'Sapta Dhara' of strength before the nation. In the coming 5 to 7 years, what could not be achieved in the last 5 to 7 decades, through the prowess and power of this Sapta Dhara, we will give the nation new heights, new momentum, and the capability to surpass new goals. Alongside this, the power and potential of our youth will be fully harnessed and integrated into nation-building..." 08:39 (IST) Aug 15 ‘Some people gain joy by keeping nation terrified’: PM Modi in I-Day address Addressing the nation on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said, "In the last 10-12 years, we have faced many dangers. As soon as we emerged from Covid, there was news of wars that started to arise from Ukraine side and West Asia. An atmosphere of tension prevailed. God knows what all the predictions the predictors made! Some people gain joy in keeping the nation terrified by spreading rumours that vaccines will not be available, petrol, diesel, and fertilizer will not be available in the country. Some people were gaining joy from creating an atmosphere of anxiousness in the country." 08:36 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day 2026: PM Modi on 'Sapta Dhara' Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, "The second power of this Sapta Dhara is Agriculture and Food Production, alongside massive Food Processing... The third power of Sapta Dhara is Technology and Innovation... The fourth power of Sapta Dhara is Gati Shakti... The fifth power of Sapta Dhara is Raksha Shakti... The sixth power of Sapta Dhara is the Green Economy and Blue Economy, which also creates green jobs... The seventh stream of our Sapta Dhara—which holds immense significance for the world—is India's Soft Power..." 08:34 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day: PM Modi outlines 'Sapt Dhara' roadmap for India's transformation Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, "The second power of this Sapta Dhara is Agriculture and Food Production, alongside massive Food Processing... The third power of Sapta Dhara is Technology and Innovation... The fourth power of Sapta Dhara is Gati Shakti... The fifth power of Sapta Dhara is Raksha Shakti... The sixth power of Sapta Dhara is the Green Economy and Blue Economy, which also creates green jobs... The seventh stream of our Sapta Dhara—which holds immense significance for the world—is India's Soft Power..." 08:31 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day: PM Modi outlines ‘Sapt Dhara’ roadmap for India’s transformation Addressing the nation from ramparts of Red Fort, PM Modi, said, "Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I call upon the nation to harness the 'Sapt Dhara... the seven streams of strength. In the next five to seven years, we will achieve what could not be achieved in the past five to seven decades. With the strength and potential of 'Sapt Dhara', we will take the nation to new heights, give it new momentum, and empower it to achieve and surpass new goals. Alongside this, the immense potential of our youth will be fully harnessed in nation-building. Their energy, talent and strength will be brought together and channelled towards building a stronger and more developed India." 08:27 (IST) Aug 15 ‘We are surging ahead rapidly’: PM Modi on India’s journey since 2014 From the ramparts of the Red Fort, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, "The country gained independence—independence accompanied by many dreams. Yet, we failed to pick up pace or gather momentum. We remained mired in an attitude of 'hoti hai,' 'chalti hai,' 'ho jaega,' or 'dekha jaega.' By 2014, the entire world had relegated us to the ranks of the "Fragile Five." Amidst that, over the last 12 years, India has gathered new momentum. We are surging ahead rapidly, and the resolve of our 1.4 billion citizens is such that nothing can now halt our collective determination and capability..." 08:22 (IST) Aug 15 'We must become self-reliant': PM Modi on 80th Independence Day Addressing the nation on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said, "We must become self-reliant and protect our interests. Today, every Indian is getting connected with initiatives of Make in India, Swadeshi, Vocal for Local." 08:17 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day 2026: RSS chief hoists tricolour at RSS headquarters in Nagpur RSS Sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat hoists the tricolour at RSS Headquarters in Nagpur on the occasion of Independence Day. 08:13 (IST) Aug 15 'Countless citizens propelled nation to new heights': PM Modi in I-Day address From the ramparts of the Red Fort, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, "... Over the past 12 years, countless citizens—whether Dalits, the downtrodden, the marginalized, or tribals; whether rural or urban dwellers; the poor or the middle class; youth or the elderly; women or men; from the North, South, East, or West—have all strived in every possible way, with unwavering resolve and dedication, to propel the nation to new heights. I respectfully acknowledge these efforts." 08:12 (IST) Aug 15 We have set target of 200 GW nuclear energy, setting up 5 new nuclear reactors. #### PM Modi 35 More Updates Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday expressed confidence that India will become a developed nation by 2047 and urged citizens to work together to realise the dream of a Viksit Bharat. Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on India’s 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India has set an ambitious goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047 and that the world is watching the country’s journey. "The whole country is moving forward with a new resolve. India has also dreamt big--and that is the dream of becoming a developed nation by 2047. Viksit Bharat will be realised in 2047. When we (the country) pledge to become Viksit, the world also watches us. When the world's most populous country takes the resolution to become a developed nation, it becomes an introduction of our courage, and the world is compelled to look at us with a different perspective," PM Modi said. The Prime Minister called on citizens to dream big and work with determination to turn those dreams into reality. "A nation becomes great and achieves its goals when it moves forward driven by its dreams, its resolve, and its inherent strength. Small dreams will no longer suffice. We must dream big, for big dreams expand our thinking and broaden the horizons of our vision. Our resolve must be steadfast; when our resolve is firm, the capacity to carve a path forward--even amidst difficulties and disasters--naturally emerges," he said. "Small dreams will no longer suffice. We must dream big, because big dreams expand our thinking, broadening the horizons of our thoughts," he added. PM Modi also described the full rendition of ‘Vande Mataram’ at the Red Fort as a historic moment, noting that it was being played there on August 15 for the first time since Independence. "For everyone present at this ceremony today, this is also a historic moment. For the first time since independence, 'Vande Mataram' is resounding at the Red Fort on August 15th. The chant of 'Vande Mataram' resonates in every heart. Today, the Tricolour flies in every home and dwells in every mind; the nation is moving forward with enthusiasm and zeal, embracing new resolutions," the PM said. Highlighting India’s economic growth, PM Modi said the country had moved beyond the "Fragile Five" phase to become a major and fast-growing economy. "We were in the Fragile Five. Now we are a major and fast-growing economy. We could not push ourselves earlier. We were stuck," the PM said. Speaking about India’s defence manufacturing capabilities, PM Modi said defence production has increased fourfold over the past 12 years.

overview.title: Transcript: PM Narendra Modi Speech at 2026 Independence Day, Red Fort
overview.content: Read the full transcript of India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks (translated to English) at 80th Independence Day from the historic Red Fort in New Delhi, August 15, 2026. [TRANSLATED USING SARVAM AI) ## Tribute to Freedom Fighters and Vande Mataram at 150 Years PRIME MINISTER NARENDRA MODI: Fellow citizens, today we are all celebrating the 80th Independence Day. Today, the heartbeat of every heart echoes with the sound of “Vande Mataram.” Today, every home is the tricolour, every mind is the tricolour, and the country is moving forward with enthusiasm and excitement, with new resolutions. Many, many best wishes to all of you on Independence Day. Today, we remember with reverence those great sons who made the ultimate sacrifice for the freedom of the country. With their penance, sacrifice, and dedication, with the sole aim of freedom, they spent their entire lives in service of the nation. Today, I respectfully salute all the freedom fighters, including the revered Bapu, and the great revolutionaries who awakened the great tradition of sacrifice. Today, for all those present at this ceremony, it is also a historic moment — after independence, for the first time on August 15, “Vande Mataram” is echoing at the Red Fort. As we, the people of this country, celebrate 150 years of Vande Mataram, what could be a greater occasion than this? ## Solidarity with Flood-Affected Families My dear countrymen, in recent days, some parts of the country have been affected by floods and landslides. Many families have been affected. We fully understand their pain and suffering. I assure the affected families that we, and the entire country, stand with them. ## Big Dreams, Firm Resolutions My dear countrymen, any nation becomes great and achieves its goals when it moves forward on the strength of its dreams, its resolutions, and its capabilities. We cannot live with small dreams anymore. We need big dreams, because big dreams broaden our thinking and expand the horizon of our vision. Our resolutions must be firm — when a resolution is firm, the ability to find a way through difficulties emerges within us. And our resolutions must also be high, because when dreams are high and resolutions are high, the height of our capabilities also increases. The height of our efforts also increases, and only then can we realize our dreams. My dear countrymen, today India has also seen a very big dream — a dream seen with firm resolve, a dream to touch new heights. That dream is: when we mark 100 years of independence, in 2047, we will be a developed India. We have to achieve this goal through the efforts of 1.4 billion countrymen. And when the country with the largest population in the world takes a pledge to develop, it becomes a symbol of our courage in the eyes of the world. The world is forced to change its perspective towards us. ## Twelve Years of Progress Countrymen, I am not saying this lightly. In the last 12 years, crores of citizens of the country — Dalits, victims, the deprived, tribals, villagers, city dwellers, the poor, the middle class, youth, elderly, women and men, from North, South, East, and West — everyone has made every effort, with dedication, with a single resolve, to take the country to new heights. I respectfully acknowledge their efforts, and the result is this: in such a short time, 250 million countrymen have overcome poverty and emerged from it. It is the result of these countrymen’s efforts that, from being counted once among the “Fragile Five,” within 12 years we have become the fastest-growing major economy. Friends, we became independent with many dreams, but we couldn’t gain momentum, we couldn’t pick up speed. It happens, it goes on, we thought — it will happen, it will be seen. We remained lost in that. By 2014, the whole world had already placed us among the “Fragile Five.” In such times, over the last 12 years, India has gained new momentum. We are moving forward at a fast pace, and the countrymen have resolved that now it is impossible to stop the resolve and strength of 1.4 billion countrymen. Fellow countrymen, in the last 12 years, defense production has increased by almost four times. Khadi and village industries production has increased by almost five times. Electronic manufacturing has increased by almost seven times. The construction of modern railway coaches has increased by twenty-one times. Mobile phone production has increased by thirty-three times. Not only that, keeping pace with the modern era, we have also raised our flag in the world of digital innovation. Internet users have increased by almost four times. The number of patent grants has increased by four times. Digital transactions have increased by a hundred times. We have worked with the same seriousness towards the facilities of the common man. Every year, on average, tap water connections have been provided 15 times faster. Every year, gas connections have been provided at a rate 6 times faster. Every year, toilets for the poor have been built at a rate 4 times faster. Every year, houses have been provided to the poor at a rate 3 times faster. The country has also brought about many changes in governance. Thousands of compliances have been abolished. We abolished hundreds of old laws — the 21st century cannot march on the laws of the previous century. We expanded the metro for modern infrastructure. We strengthened public transport. The speed at which we worked, the scale at which we worked — this pace, this expansion, this achievement — the last decade has seen for the first time since independence. And when so many achievements are in front of us, and such a fast pace is visible, the strength of the countrymen is revealed every moment. The resolution to become a developed India in 2047 can never remain incomplete. All these figures testify that we are going to move forward. ## The Path of Self-Reliance My dear countrymen, for this, self-confidence is needed, self-respect is needed, and along with that, it is very important to have a self-reliant India. ## Semiconductors and Critical Minerals My dear countrymen, I will give you an example of semiconductors. After the country became independent, there was talk of semiconductors in the world, and talk about it here too. But we could not take any big plan for semiconductors forward. What is the situation today? In today’s digital world, in today’s technology, we understand the importance of chips — in electronic goods, in medical equipment, in transportation. Chips are essential in everything, and without them, a situation has arisen where the world could come to a standstill. That is why India has embarked on a major semiconductor plan towards becoming self-reliant. Three semiconductor plants have already started production, and I have been told that exports from there have already begun. I want to tell the countrymen that in the coming years, five to eight more semiconductor plants are going to start very soon. This is self-reliant India — it gives us the highway to move towards a developed India. My dear countrymen, a similar discussion is going on about critical minerals. The entire technology ecosystem is dependent on critical minerals, and India is also engaged in securing itself in this area. We have launched the National Critical Minerals Mission. We have announced a critical minerals corridor. Agreements are being made with many countries, and many countries around the world are now starting to trust India regarding critical minerals. ## Energy Security and Nuclear Power My dear countrymen, like semiconductors and critical minerals, the importance of energy is also increasing as we move in the direction the world is moving. It is now difficult to run a new world without energy — be it AI or data centers, we will need large amounts of electricity. Energy security is the demand of our time, and that is why we have already taken strong steps, one after the other, in that direction. A major medium of energy security is nuclear energy. We have passed the Nuclear Energy Act in Parliament and have decided on the path to move towards a new goal. By 2047, we are moving with the goal of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power. Within this decade, we are moving with the goal of starting five new nuclear reactors. This year, India has achieved a significant milestone by mastering fast breeder nuclear technology, and as a result, we have taken a major step towards becoming self-reliant in nuclear fuel. ## Unlocking Our Own Resources My dear countrymen, sometimes the country does not stop due to a lack of resources — the reason for stopping is the limitations of thinking. When thinking becomes confined within boundaries, we cannot even recognize our own potential. Today, the country has to depend on crude oil. This is due to our wrong thinking of the past. You will be surprised to know that we had declared 99% of our coastline as a “No Go Area.” We ourselves decided not to explore inside the sea. This was a poverty of thought. We decided this could not go on, and we opened up that 99% from “No Go Areas” to “Go Ahead Areas.” Now we are inclined to explore even inside the sea and are trying to find new reserves. Last year, taking an important step in the same direction, we announced “Samudra Manthan.” Recently, we have decided to allocate ₹85,000 crore for this work and speed it up. ## Expanding Alternative Energy My dear countrymen, I said that it is very important for us to put all our energy towards alternative sources as well, and India is working rapidly in this direction. Before 2014 — 12 years ago from today — only 70 cities in our country had piped gas supply. In 12 years, we have expanded this from 70 cities to 700 cities. This is speed, this is expansion. Before 2014, hardly 20-22 lakh houses had piped gas. Today, the work of providing piped gas is being done in three-and-a-quarter crore houses. Twelve years ago, the capacity of solar energy in the country was only 2 gigawatts. Today, we have achieved the target of 160 gigawatts. My dear countrymen, I would like to share another piece of information. We have focused equally on ensuring that the middle class and ordinary families in the country benefit from this. We launched the PM Surya Ghar Free Electricity Scheme, and today I am satisfied that in such a short time, we have crossed the figure of 5 million homes with solar energy, and it is progressing rapidly. As a result, the electricity bills of thousands of homes have become zero, and thousands of homes are earning by selling their surplus electricity. For this work, the government is providing ₹80,000 to each family. ## Railway Electrification and the Hydrogen Train My dear countrymen, you will be surprised to know this. The electrification of our railway system started in our country in 1925, but in the 90 years from 1925, only 30% of the railway was electrified. See our speed over those 90 years — just 30%. We have completed the remaining work within just one decade. 30% in 90 years, 70% in 10 years — this is how the work happens. Because of this, the diesel that we had to bring from outside has been saved. Our trains now run on electricity, and the environment has started to benefit. My dear countrymen, we have not stopped here. We do not want to be left behind in the world. You must have heard the news in the past few days — India has also touched this new field of fuel. The country has started its first hydrogen-powered train, and I am happy that it is the longest and most powerful such train. India has also hoisted its flag in the field of hydrogen trains in the world. ## Overcoming Global Crises Fellow citizens, for the last 10-12 years, we have been continuously working to achieve the target of 2047, proving ourselves step by step. We never thought we would have to face so many difficulties along the way. In these 12 years, we have faced numerous crises. The global pandemic like Covid had put the whole world in worry — all systems had collapsed. As we emerged from Covid, news of war-like situations started to arrive. Everywhere, from Ukraine to West Asia, there was an atmosphere of tension. And who knows how many soothsayers made announcements to scare the country, to keep the country terrified and worried. Some people find pleasure in spreading fear — “the vaccine will not be available,” “people will not survive Covid,” “nothing is going to happen.” When the West Asia crisis came, they said, “there will be no petrol at the pump, no gas, no diesel, no fertilizer” — spreading fear all over. Some people were enjoying scaring the people of India, terrifying them, drowning them in worry. But the country has seen that the well-thought-out plans of the last 10-12 years have borne fruit, and despite such a big crisis, the preparations India had made, taking the mantra of self-reliance as our refuge, took us forward step by step. We did not anticipate this crisis, but at that time, all our preparations came in handy. Today, the country has gas, petrol, and urea. We are standing on our own strength, moving forward. ## Shielding Farmers from Global Price Shocks My dear countrymen, these crises in the world have affected everyone; we are not untouched either. The price of urea has reached ₹3,000 per bag in the world market. Even today, we are not forcing the farmers of my country to bear that burden — the government is carrying that burden on its shoulders, and the urea bag that costs ₹3,000 in the world, we give to our farmers for only ₹300. Not only that, DAP has reached ₹5,000 in the world market today, but so that the farmers of my country do not face any problem, we are still working to provide DAP for ₹1,350. ## India’s Rising Global Standing My dear countrymen, there was a time when, as I was talking about self-reliance, some people sitting in air-conditioned chambers were telling us what would happen with globalization. But the world is seeing that over the last decade, it seems the world itself has stopped talking about globalization. Every country in the world has turned inward towards its own priorities. Unfortunately, in this time of crisis, some, to show their strength, have played the game of weaponizing resources — petrol, diesel, fertilizers, medicines, technology, chips, and even land are being weaponized. If we had not taken the mantra of self-reliance and walked in the right direction for these 10 years, imagine how difficult it would have been to face such challenges. Our preparations are continuously increasing. My dear countrymen, on the other hand, today India’s global profile is rising. India is becoming a recognized and respected country in the eyes of the world. India has a stable political mandate, a stable government, a vibrant democracy, a strong judicial system, and we all have India’s Constitution to guide us. The world has started to recognize our capabilities, and that is why, after 2014, we have entered Free Trade Agreements with almost 40 countries. ## Opportunities for MSMEs and Exports Look — what a big opportunity has come! These trade agreements are a very big opportunity, and that is why I would especially like to tell my MSMEs that we should not miss this opportunity. We have to reach the world — everything from India’s products should reach the world market, whether it is our textiles, our machinery, or our medicines. We should not miss this opportunity, but we must surpass global parameters. We must give the world what it needs, at competitive prices, and with quality. From Ludhiana in Punjab to Tirupur in Tamil Nadu, our textile sector can reach the world. Not only that, from Kerala to Gujarat, and from Tamil Nadu to Bengal — along our coastline, our fishermen brothers and sisters, due to these FTAs, have great potential for the export of our shrimp and seafood to the world. I would like to see us take advantage of this opportunity as we move forward. ## Building on a Strong Foundation My dear countrymen, the goal of 2047, of a developed India, stands on this strong foundation — the strength that the countrymen have shown over the last 10-12 years. A quarter of a century has passed, and the next quarter is extremely important for us. Now we cannot stop; our pace cannot stop. Our direction has been determined; we have to achieve it and sustain it. That is why we have to change our work culture, and while changing it, we also have to change our thinking. The pace of work that was not achieved in five to seven decades, we have to achieve in the coming 5-7 years. I have faith in the youth of my country, in the young people, in the mothers and sisters, in the farmers, in the laborers, that we can realize this dream. That is why we also have to accelerate the pace of reform. Reform is not a compulsion for us — reform is a conviction. Out of conviction, we have embarked on the reform express, and we are going to move towards the next level of reform in the coming days as well. Government, society, industry, producers, farmers — everyone has to reform their traditional systems, reform our thinking, reform our goals, and move forward with a definite direction. ## The Seven Streams (Sapt Dhara) of National Power Today, I would also like to remember the era when we knew, understood, and heard about India’s strength as the seven rivers. Now, to build a developed India, we need a new stream. Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the seven streams of power before the country. In the coming 5-7 years, we will give the country new heights and new momentum with the strength of these seven streams — something that has not happened in the last 5-7 decades — and we will build the strength to achieve new goals. Along with this, the strength of the country’s youth will be fully utilized in nation-building. ### 1. Manufacturing Power My dear countrymen, we have to take the manufacturing sector far ahead. Along with increasing production, we have to make small parts as well as big products. We should have a complete value chain — we need components, and we also need complete manufacturing of finished products. From design to manufacturing, India has to become a reliable center of the global supply chain. I want to emphasize three things to my brothers and sisters in the field of manufacturing: this is the opportunity of the times, and we should not let it go. We have to meet global standards in terms of cost, quality, and scale. Our factories should be competitive, our products should be user-friendly, our packaging should be attractive to the people of the world, and zero-defect, precision manufacturing should become our identity. Our identity in the global market should be based on credibility and quality — no compromise on quality. Our mantra should be quality, quality, quality. This will become our global brand value. ### 2. Agriculture and Food Production My dear countrymen, the second stream of the Sapt Dhara is agriculture and food processing. We have to move forward in this direction. The world’s markets are now open to our farmers because of our FTAs, and we are getting a very big market. We have to reach there — we have to go from the field to the export market. Whether it is our traditional food, our millets, our spices, or our fruits and flowers — is there anything we don’t have? These should become global brands. Our farmers will give strength to chemical-free farming, and demand for it in the world is going to increase further. If our agro products meet global parameters in every way, we will be able to reach the world easily. ### 3. Technology and Innovation The third stream of the Sapt Dhara is technology and innovation. Today’s era belongs to AI, quantum computing, space, robotics, and data centers. A completely new field has opened up, and emerging technology is challenging us every moment. We should not let the country become a market for the world — we have to become a hub of innovation. We have made our mark with UPI and digital public infrastructure, and we have put our strength to the test. Now we have to take India’s digital public technology to every corner of the world. We have to lead in next-generation communication technology — Made in India 6G should reach every corner. This should be our goal, and we should speed up our efforts towards it. ### 4. Gati Shakti (Momentum) The fourth stream of the Sapt Dhara is Gati Shakti. This momentum requires us to emphasize seamless, fast connectivity within the country. We need to connect cities with high-speed rail, we need modern highways, we need inland waterways, we need airports, and we need multimodal logistics. Our ports need to be more than just places to unload and operate goods — we don’t want world ships to simply anchor here; we need to move our ports towards port-led development and growth. ### 5. Defense Strength Our fifth stream is defense strength. It is important to become self-reliant in defense in every way. India has experienced it, the world has experienced it — there is no other option. While the world thinks only of itself, India cannot remain a market for the world. We must become self-reliant in defense by developing next-generation defense technology and move forward with the goal of becoming a global supplier. We need to develop drone and counter-drone systems, and we need to take leadership in hypersonic defense technologies. Cyber security is also becoming a challenge for every home today — that too is a field of defense in which we can channel the potential of our youth for the country and the world. ### 6. Green and Blue Economy Our sixth stream of the Sapt Dhara is the green economy and the blue economy, which also give birth to green jobs. We need to advance green hydrogen, renewable energy, energy storage, green mobility, and green manufacturing on a global scale. While the world keeps talking about global warming, we need to find solutions — India has embarked on a green movement with great potential. India also has a great opportunity in the blue economy. We have a very long coastline, and there are great opportunities in fisheries, coastal tourism, and ocean technology — areas in which we can move forward. ### 7. Soft Power My dear countrymen, our seventh stream is India’s soft power. Yoga has kept the whole world connected with India — it is becoming an energy for the world and a major reason for trust in India. India has centers of faith, India has Ayurveda, and through our holistic healthcare system, the “Heal in India” movement, we can carry our strength to the world. Be it handicrafts, culture, our films, or our creative world — VFX, animation, gaming, digital content — India can show its standing in the creative world. We have to develop it as a global strength. India has given great strength to the Wave Summit, the World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit, and it will introduce India’s soft power and creative world to the globe. India has vast wildlife resources — we have more than 100 national parks. There is a lot of potential, but we are falling short in attracting foreign tourists. We have a chance to attract tourists from around the world through our soft power, and we will do this work in the times ahead. The world’s sports events are also a great attraction — why not host them in India? The events economy is growing, and it is an attraction for the youth of the country. Everyone in the world wants to hold their events on the soil of India at some point. This is a great opportunity, and we need to establish systems to harness it. ## A Holistic Vision for Global Leadership Friends, the purpose of these seven powers of the Sapt Dhara is not just progress in one sector. With a holistic approach, we need to work towards surpassing the scale of the goals and ambitions we are pursuing. My dear countrymen, I want to connect the country’s power with the world. A country is not just a government — a country means every citizen is connected. We hear a lot about Fortune 500 companies. Why shouldn’t 50 of them be Indian companies? Why shouldn’t this be our goal? Today, the banking sector is flourishing — why shouldn’t India’s banks also be among the top banks in the world? India should have one of the top five banks globally. In the pharma sector, we have done a lot of work, but the demand of the time is that one or two Indian pharma companies should also resonate among the world’s top five pharma companies. There are law firms, there are rating agencies — isn’t it the demand of the time that we now aim for global leadership? We have talent, we have capability, we have a long history, and we have command over languages. We should reach the world. Why shouldn’t any of our consulting firms or accounting firms be among the top firms in the world? India’s technology companies should be at the forefront globally — this should be our goal. We should have brands that attract the world, brands that become the identity of our country and a destination for the world. We have to work in that direction. For this, I want to tell the state governments and local self-government institutions — and it is also the responsibility of the Government of India — to accelerate the pace of our reforms. We have to develop our systems in line with the goal of 2047. We cannot be guided by the policies and regulations of the past; we have to formulate policies according to the dreams of the future. I am fully confident that by working hard on this path, we will achieve the dream of a developed India. The central government, state governments, and industry all have to move forward together, continuing to bring reforms — not out of compulsion, but out of conviction, to achieve our goal. ## Empowering India’s Youth My dear countrymen, when I talk about taking the country forward at a fast pace, who is the biggest beneficiary of all these efforts? The youth of my country. The youth have a very big role in the journey of a developed India, and they are also its biggest beneficiaries. That is why we have to take the goal of a developed India forward with the youth as our top priority. Friends, a lot has happened in this direction over the last 10-12 years. Through the Startup India campaign, more than 2.5 lakh registered startups have been formed across the country. The Government of India has announced a ₹1 lakh crore Innovation Fund. I want to tell the youth of the country: come with your dreams, we will not let there be a shortage of resources. New opportunities for research emerged, and cheap digital data empowered the youth of Digital India. If there’s cheap data anywhere in the world, it’s on Indian soil. We created Skill India as a national program, opened up the space sector, created the National Drone Policy, and created the Khelo India policy. There was no education policy for 35 years — we brought in a new one, and middle-class families have benefited from it. Friends, from 2004 to 2014, there were fewer than 350 universities in our country. Today, within 10-12 years, about 650 new universities have been added, and we are reaching a figure of about 1,000. Before 2014, there were only 400 medical seats; today, there are almost 850 medical seats. Now, foreign universities are also coming to Indian soil, and our youth can get a foreign university degree right here in India. We are working to attract young minds to technology from childhood, and that is why we have handed over more than 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs to young children, to inspire innovation and technology from an early age. Our youth have opened many avenues in startups — India’s private space startups, run by youth with an average age of 28 years, launched their first satellite and rocket successfully on their very first trial. Today, there are more than 2.5 lakh registered startups. We recently held the AI Impact Summit. The expansion of AI is growing very rapidly, and from the Red Fort, I want to make an announcement for the youth of the country: we have decided that in the coming year, we will work to train 10 million youth in AI skills, so that the youth of our country have the ability to lead in the world of AI as well. ## The Rise of the Bio-Economy and Electric Vehicles My friends, the bio-economy is a new field. Before 2014, it was worth only ₹60,000 crore. Look at the wonders my country’s youth have done — when policies are right and goals are clear, they have shown their strength. The bio-economy business that was ₹60,000 crore before 2014 has reached ₹20 lakh crore today. In 2009-10, only one-and-a-half lakh electric vehicles were sold in our country. In 2025-26, 2.5 million electric vehicles have been sold. ## Aviation, Drones, and New Opportunities My dear countrymen, the aviation sector is also moving forward very fast for my youth. New airports, new routes, and new employment opportunities are being created in maintenance and overhaul work, providing a large amount of skilled manpower with work in the country. We have achieved success in making Made in India airplanes — the Made in India Defense Transport Aircraft, the C-295, has already taken its first successful flight. Drones have also done great work for the youth of this country. The Swamitva Yojana is being made successful in villages through drones. About 3.25 crore families have benefited from the Swamitva Yojana, and assets worth ₹140 lakh crore have been unlocked as a result, enabling people to get loans from banks and start their own businesses. ## Free Coaching for the Middle Class My dear countrymen, our middle-class families carry a very big burden — the competition of coaching classes. Every parent feels that if they do not send their child to a coaching class, they are failing their family. We are concerned about the thousands of crores of rupees spent by poor and middle-class families on this, and we want to save them from this burden, so that children can stay close to their families and be taken care of, without the financial strain falling on the household. That is why we have decided to provide free online coaching for various exams for the youth. We have digital public infrastructure, excellent talent, and teachers. By combining these resources, we are going to build a complete network to provide free coaching to the youth of the country. ## India’s Sporting Ambitions My dear countrymen, I have always said, let those who wish to play, play. Today, India is making its place in the world of sports. Now, India’s national anthem is played on sports podiums; India’s tricolour flag is seen waving. The TOPS scheme has achieved great success. Khelo India Games, University Games, Winter Games, Beach Games, sports infrastructure, coaching, sports medicine, and sports nutrition — India is now moving forward on all fronts related to sports. India’s performance in the world of sports is improving, and we are moving forward as a strong contender to host the Olympics in 2036. India is also going to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030. My friends, in the world of Olympic sports, there are about 40 types of games and roughly 250 to 350 competitions. You will be saddened to know, my countrymen — I challenge you, I appeal to you, I want your help — that in these 250-300 competitions, India has no presence in two-thirds of the games. We don’t qualify. We have decided that for the Olympics in 2036, which we hope to host in India, we want to focus especially on the disciplines in which India does not play or qualify today. Three-quarters of the share is waiting for us, and India will emphasize this. For this, we also want to run a talent-hunt campaign. If we need players for 2036, we need to focus on the youth of today — the sons and daughters aged 5, 10, and 15. A talent-hunt campaign will be conducted in every village, city, and school to find sporting talent in children aged 5 to 15. Once identified, they will be given special training to become good players for the country. ## A Drug-Free India My dear youth, addiction is becoming a major crisis for the country and its young people. A drug-free India should be our collective responsibility. For our bright future, our young generation should be strong, and our youth’s strength should be useful to our country. Recently, volunteers from My Bharat, NGOs, social and cultural organizations, and spiritual leaders of the country jointly decided on a 100-week program for a drug-free India. I want to tell every family to be a part of this campaign — join it, and help fulfill the dream of a drug-free India. ## Eliminating Naxalism and Intellectual Extremism My dear countrymen, it is very important to eliminate the decades-old challenges of the 21st century. Naxalism and Maoism have destroyed the future of millions of youth, snatching mothers’ sons away from them, ruining lives and shattering the dreams of every parent. This Naxalism had captured a large and populous part of India for four decades — at gunpoint, tearing apart the Constitution. In defense of the common citizens of the country, more than 3,500 of our police and security force personnel have been martyred — more than the number of soldiers who die in war. Our police personnel had to risk their lives so that the common man could be safe. This Naxalism had turned the earth into a land of blood. In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity, we vowed that we would free the country from Naxalism. Today, I am happy that Naxalite-Maoist violence, even in its last breath, no longer has the strength to survive. We are moving towards completely eradicating it. In the very areas where Naxalites used to fire bullets, where the earth used to be stained with blood, today the tricolour of development, trust, and effort is waving. But we are not underestimating this challenge — we need to be even more careful. For years, people with Maoist ideologies were ensconced in the corridors of power, even influencing policies through government committees as advisors. We have succeeded in eradicating the armed Naxalites in the forests and freeing the country from that crisis. But while the armed Naxalites are gone, the intellectual Naxalites are still looking for opportunities — searching for ways to spread violence and anarchy in society, resorting to various tactics to mislead people. These intellectual Naxalites must be identified, they must be isolated, and the country’s young generation must be connected to the mainstream of nation-building. ## Strengthening National and Civil Defense My dear countrymen, it is our responsibility to create a safe India. Whether the challenge is within the border or beyond, India is ready for every situation. Today, the nature of war is changing. War is no longer fought only at the border — infrastructure like refineries, banking systems, and data centers are being targeted, and factories are being destroyed in new forms of conflict. We had announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra last year, and work is progressing very fast. Today, our defense exports have increased by about 50 times, and our weapons are reaching nearly 100 countries. India’s prestige is steadily increasing on the global stage. In these changing times, we need to strengthen our weaponry and increase the capabilities of our military forces. But along with that, we also need to prepare our citizens. The civil defense systems that developed in our country, in line with the wars of the last century, have become outdated. That is why I am announcing from the Red Fort today that we will build a vibrant network of civil defense in the coming days, familiarizing citizens with modern systems that can protect them from modern crises. We are going to create a very large voluntary civil defense force to help overcome modern challenges. ## Celebrating the Power of Women My dear countrymen, in nation-building today, the contribution of our sisters and daughters has become a great source of inspiration for all of us. Whether it is fighter jets or civil aviation, our daughters are at the forefront. Whether it is the sports field, our daughters are ahead. Whether it is admission to STEM education, our daughters are leading. Girls have emerged, showing the ability to lead the country’s army with great pride. I recently visited a semiconductor plant in Sanand, where tribal girls from different corners of the country were working — girls from villages where they didn’t even know what a passport was. Those girls went abroad for training and came back to work in chip manufacturing, and the confidence they showed truly impressed me. Today, we had set a goal of making 3 crore sisters “Lakhpati Didis,” and we have exceeded it. Now we are moving forward with the goal of making 6 crore Lakhpati Didis — meaning a very big change is coming to the rural economy through the power of mothers. My dear countrymen, today, in Panchayats, Municipalities, and Municipal Corporations, a large number of our women are becoming public representatives, guiding the country, solving problems, and providing capable leadership. Keeping this in mind, we passed the Nari Shakti Vandan Act in Parliament. However, for one reason or another, this dream had fallen victim to the arena of politics for the past 40 years. Today, I stand before all the political parties of the country, under the shade of the tricolour flag from the ramparts of the Red Fort, and I appeal to you: come forward and honor the power of our women as soon as possible. Our mothers and sisters should get 33% representation in the Legislative Assemblies and the Lok Sabha, and contribute to shaping India’s policies. This is the demand of the time. I again urge all political parties: come forward, implement women’s reservation, and give rights to my mothers and sisters. ## Social Security and Healthcare for All My dear countrymen, the resolution of a developed India will only be fulfilled when development reaches the last person. Before 2014, only 25 crore people had social security cover. In the last decade, we have extended social security to 100 crore countrymen — a task that would have taken five to seven decades otherwise. With the Ayushman Bharat Yojana, even elderly people of 70 years are now getting free medical treatment up to ₹5 lakh. Crores of families have benefited greatly from this, and because of the Ayushman card, ₹2 lakh crore that would have been spent on medicines and operations is being saved for poor and middle-class families. ## A Call for Participation in the Census My dear countrymen, today I need your help with a task, and I am asking all of you, especially the youth, to take the lead. Just one or two hours of your time will give great strength to the country. These days, census work is going on in the country. Counting alone doesn’t achieve results with just figures — policies and plans are made from its nuances, and the country prepares its roadmap for moving forward. That is why having accurate information is very important. Sometimes the representatives who come from the government are in a hurry, and mistakes happen with spellings or details, which creates difficulties in getting the final results right. Now that technology is available, a decision has been made this time that you can fill in your own information for the census yourself, using your mobile phone. Later, an officer or representative will come to discuss it with you, but if you sit with your family and complete your registration digitally, there will be no mistakes in the details or spellings. The more accurate the information you provide, the more it will help the country move forward. I tell the youth of the country: sit with your family members, understand the entire form, first fill it out on paper, correct any mistakes, and then upload it digitally. This will save the country’s time and resources for the right work, and that is why I urge the youth of my country to actively participate in this census exercise. ## A Shared Resolve for a Developed India My dear countrymen, I have spoken of the seven vital streams from the Red Fort. These seven streams will give the country great strength to move forward with self-respect and with the ability to achieve its goals. We have to keep eradicating the mentality of slavery every moment. The dream of India that Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose saw, that Baba Saheb Ambedkar saw, that Pandit Nehru saw, that Sardar Patel, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru saw, that Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee saw, that Bhagwan Birsa Munda saw, that Jyotiba Phule saw — taking inspiration from all of them, we move forward. Come, let us reiterate this resolve: let the nation’s interest be above our own, and let duty be our identity. The time is ours, the opportunity is ours, the resolve is ours. Come, let’s turn dreams into resolutions, resolutions into capabilities, and capabilities into success. Let us make every step a step towards development. Let us join hands, mind to mind, staying connected to the goal — with one lamp, thousands of lamps will light up. Come, let us build a developed India together. With this one feeling, many, many best wishes to all of you on this auspicious festival. Say with me — “Bharat Mata Ki Jai! Bharat Mata Ki Jai! Bharat Mata Ki Jai! Vande Mataram! Vande Mataram! Vande Mataram!” Thank you very much. ### Related Posts * Transcript: Ben Shapiro Interview on PBD Podcast #842 * Transcript: Krystal Ball and Saagar Enjeti Interview on The Weekly Show * Transcript of Catherine Austin Fitts Interview on Tucker Carlson Show * Transcript: President Trump Remarks at Oval Office Vaccine Event * Transcript of Hunter Biden Interview on Tucker Carlson Show

overview.title: 80th Independence Day Live Updates: 80th Independence Day Celebrations Mark 150 Years Of 'Vande Mataram'
overview.content: 2 hours ago Aug 15, 2026 **80th Independence Day Live Updates:** The nation commemorated the 80th Independence Day on August 15, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi leading the celebrations at the Red Fort complex here amid patriotic fervour and multi-layer security. For the first time, the national song, 'Vande Mataram', was rendered during the celebrations at the Red Fort. An Army band played the tune of 'Vande Mataram' as the guests present on the occasion sang the national song. This was followed by the prime minister hoisting the national flag, and then the National Anthem was recited. The National Anthem rendition was synchronised with the 21-gun salute by the gunners of the 1721 Field Battery (Ceremonial), utilising the indigenous 105mm Light Field Guns. Floral decoration on the ramparts depicted the national flag at the centre, flanked by 'Vande Mataram' in Hindi. After the flag hoisting, the tricolour received a 'Rashtriya Salute'. Following this, flower petals were showered at the venue by two Mi-17 helicopters of the Indian Air Force -- one trooping the national flag and the other carrying a flag depicting 'Vande Mataram'. ## **Here Are The 80th Independence Day Celebration LIVE Updates:** Aug 15, 2026 23:31 (IST) ### Iranian President Congratulates PM Modi On Independence Day > Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian, President of the Islamic Republic of Iran, in a message to Shri Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India, congratulated him on the occasion of the 80th anniversary of the Independence of the Republic of India, describing the occasion as a valuable opportunity… pic.twitter.com/l0yQLlDjWA > > — Iran in India (@Iran\_in\_India) August 15, 2026 Aug 15, 2026 22:54 (IST) ### Far From Home, Young Indians in Paris Celebrate Independence Day Members of the Indian community organised a Tiranga celebration in Paris, drawing strong participation from the community, particularly Gen Z university students. The event was held to mark the occasion with patriotic fervour and to raise awareness against anti-India activities. Aug 15, 2026 20:30 (IST) ### Singapore President Congratulates India On Independence Day Congratulating India on its 80th Independence Day, Singapore President Tharman Shanmugaratnam said that both South Asian nations share a robust and forward-looking Comprehensive Strategic Partnership that is underpinned by close people-to-people ties. In a letter to his Indian counterpart, Draupadi Murmu, penned on August 15, President Shanmugaratnam also noted that the two countries’ cooperation is multifaceted, expanding into new areas of skills development, digitalisation, sustainability and advanced manufacturing. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 20:29 (IST) ### Indians, ‘Friends Of India’ Celebrate 80th Independence Day Across Globe From the Pacific islands and East Asia to Europe, the Gulf and the Americas, Indians and “friends of India” joined celebrations marking the country's 80th Independence Day on Saturday, as key partners including France, Russia and Australia extended greetings and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening ties with New Delhi. The celebrations unfolded across Indian missions and diaspora communities around the world, featuring flag-hoisting ceremonies, renditions of the national anthem and "Vande Mataram", cultural performances, community gatherings and a range of activities. At the centre of the global celebrations was the "Suryapath Tiranga" initiative, under which the Indian Tricolour was hoisted successively at Indian missions as the day moved across time zones, beginning in Fiji and scheduled to culminate in San Francisco. The initiative, part of the broader "Har Ghar Tiranga" campaign, sought to create a shared, continuous celebration stretching from one sunrise to the next. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 18:35 (IST) Aug 15, 2026 16:58 (IST) ### Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah Greets Indian People On 80th Independence Day Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Saturday extended greetings and best wishes to his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi and the people of India on the occasion of the country's 80th Independence Day. Shah's message comes amid Nepal's efforts to strengthen ties with India, with the Himalayan nation seeking greater economic cooperation and connectivity with its immediate neighbour. “On the occasion of India's 80th Independence Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings and best wishes to PM @narendramodi and the friendly people and Government of India,” Shah’s office said in a post on X. Shah's message also comes days after he held his first one-on-one meeting with Indian Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava on August 10, after having largely avoided such engagements with foreign diplomats since taking office. “May the deep historical ties, close people-to-people relations and cooperation between Nepal and India continue to strengthen in the years ahead,” Shah said on Saturday. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 16:23 (IST) Aug 15, 2026 15:02 (IST) ### Jammu And Kashmir Chief Minister Pays Tribute To Martyrs On Independence Day 15 Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday paid floral tributes at the Balidan Stambh here to honour the martyrs as the nation celebrated its 80th Independence Day. The chief minister laid a wreath at the memorial and observed a moment of silence as a mark of respect for those who made the supreme sacrifice in service of the nation, a government spokesperson said. Director of Police Nalin Prabhat, Kashmir Divisional Commissioner Anshul Garg and other senior officials and security personnel were present. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 15:01 (IST) ### French President Emmanuel Macron Extends Greetings On India's 80th Independence Day French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday extended his warm wishes to the people of India on the landmark occasion of the nation's 80th Independence Day. In a message posted on X, the French President wrote, "Congratulations to the Indian people on your 80th Independence Day!" > Congratulations to the Indian people on your 80th Independence Day! 🇮🇳🇫🇷 > > — Emmanuel Macron (@EmmanuelMacron) August 15, 2026 Aug 15, 2026 15:00 (IST) ### Putin Greets President Murmu, PM Modi On Independence Day Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday greeted his Indian counterpart Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the occasion of India's 80th Independence Day, expressing confidence that the constructive bilateral partnership will benefit in enhancing international security and stability. The Kremlin said in a statement that President Putin also said the bilateral relations are developing successfully in the spirit of a "particularly privileged strategic partnership." Putin is set to visit India in September to attend the BRICS Summit. "Your country is making remarkable progress in the economic, social, scientific and technological spheres, and rightfully commands considerable authority in the international arena," Putin said. "Russia-India relations are developing successfully in the spirit of a particularly privileged strategic partnership," he said and pointed out how Moscow and New Delhi are engaged in fruitful cooperation across a wide range of areas and coordinate closely within the framework of the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, BRICS, and other multilateral institutions. "I am confident that, through our joint efforts, we will continue to comprehensively strengthen the constructive Russia-India partnership for the benefit of our friendly peoples and in the interests of enhancing international security and stability," the Russian president said. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 14:59 (IST) ### BJP Accuses Kerala Of 'Bowing To Pressure' Over Omission Of Vande Mataram A political row erupted in Kerala on Saturday after Vande Mataram was not included in the state government's Independence Day function, with the BJP accusing the Congress-led UDF government of "yielding to pressure from extremist organisations." The BJP said it would launch a legal and political battle against the government over what it termed an "unconstitutional act". BJP leader Shone George told reporters that people in Kerala had witnessed "with sorrow" Chief Minister V D Satheesan "surrendering to the dictate of Jamaat-e-Islami". "We were convinced of this. Because this is not new-for the past one year, the CM has had an illicit relationship with Jamaat-e-Islami and anti-India forces, both openly and covertly in Kerala," he alleged. George said the BJP had expected Vande Mataram to be sung at the official function and alleged that the CM had failed to show "basic courtesy" by doing so. He referred to guidelines issued by the Education Department and claimed they stated that singing Vande Mataram was not mandatory. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 13:52 (IST) ### Union Ministers Extend Independence Day Greetings Union ministers on Saturday extended greetings to the people on the country's 80th Independence Day and paid tributes to freedom fighters, while calling for collective efforts to build a developed, prosperous and self-reliant India. Union Home Minister Amit Shah urged citizens to resolve to speed up the country's development. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said Independence Day is an occasion to remember the courage and sacrifice of freedom fighters, while also highlighting the responsibility of the citizens in shaping the country's future. Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari called for efforts to build a "New India" and realise the vision of an 'Atmanirbhar Bharat'. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal urged people to promote "swadeshi" and contribute to the country's progress. Health Minister JP Nadda stressed the need to strengthen national unity, integrity, brotherhood and democratic values. Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan called upon people to "live for the country" by performing their duties with honesty and dedication. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said Prime Minister Narendra Modi hoisting the national flag at the Red Fort was as memorable as Vande Mataram was played there for the first time. Education Minister Pralhad Joshi said the tricolour embodies the courage, sacrifice and spirit of the freedom fighters and urged people to renew their resolve to serve the nation and contribute towards building a stronger, more prosperous and developed India. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said the last 12 years have witnessed India's "atmavishwas, atmagaurav and atmanirbharta" ( self-confidence, self-respect and self-reliance) and highlighted the role of youth, women, farmers and workers in achieving the vision of a developed India. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 13:00 (IST) ### India Must Become Self-Reliant, Not Dependent On Others: PM Modi Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said India must not remain dependent on other countries and move towards self-reliance by strengthening its own capabilities and protecting its national interests. "We have to become self-reliant," Modi said, addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort after unfurling the national flag on the 80th Independence Day. "There are many things in the world. They are cheaper, they are readily available. But that does not build our capabilities, nor does it test our capabilities. Therefore, we must develop our own capabilities and protect our own interests," he said. PM Modi said government initiatives such as Make in India and Vocal for Local are becoming part of the thinking of every Indian. "We are moving forward with a firm resolve of Aatmanirbhar Bharat," he said. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 12:34 (IST) ### In 2047, 'Viksit Bharat' Dreams Will Be Realised Through 'Viksit Bengal': Suvendu Adhikari West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 will be realised through a prosperous West Bengal. Hoisting the national Tricolour on Independence Day here, Adhikari said West Bengal is the land of nationalism and freedom fighters such as Khudiram Bose and Matangini Hazra. "The Viksit Bharat dreams of our Prime Minister by 2047 will be realised through Viksit Paschim Banga by that year," he said. Describing Bharatiya Jana Sangh founder Syama Prasad Mookerjee as the architect of West Bengal, Adhikari said the state wants to fulfil his dreams. "Our two luminaries, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and Rabindranath Tagore, composed the national song Vande Mataram and the national anthem Jana Gana Mana respectively, which stirred the entire nation," he said. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 12:29 (IST) ### Bangladesh Extends Independence Day Wishes To India Bangladesh on Saturday extended warm greetings to the people of India on the 80th Independence Day and also paid tributes to the freedom fighters who laid down their lives for India's independence. In a post on its social media platform X, the Bangladesh High Commission to India conveyed its wishes through a multilingual Independence Day message, highlighting the themes of "Friendship, Harmony and Prosperity". "Bangladesh greets all men, women, and children in India as they celebrate eightieth Independence Day. We solemnly remember the brave souls who laid their lives in the long Freedom Movement," it posted on X. > #Bangladesh🇧🇩 greets all 🇮🇳men-women-children in #India as they celebrate eightieth #IndependenceDay. > We solemnly remember the brave souls who laid their lives in the long Freedom Movement.#Freedom #People #Youth #Tiranga pic.twitter.com/RiSmzaU4A9 > > — Bangladesh High Commission, New Delhi (@bdhc\_delhi) August 15, 2026 Aug 15, 2026 12:02 (IST) ### Independence Day celebrated in Punjab, Haryana Independence Day was celebrated with flag hoisting ceremonies across Punjab, Haryana and their common capital Chandigarh on Saturday. Punjab Governor and Union territory Chandigarh Administrator Gulab Chand Kataria hoisted the national flag at Chandigarh, while Haryana Governor Ashim Kumar Ghosh hoisted the national flag in Yamunanagar. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann hoisted the national flag at a state-level function in Ferozepur and his Haryana counterpart Nayab Singh Saini unfurled the tricolour in Hansi. Tight security arrangements were made in the two states for Independence Day events. Delivering his address on the occasion of 80th Independence Day at a state-level function in Ferozepur, Mann remembered the contribution of martyrs including freedom fighters Bhagat Singh. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 11:19 (IST) ### PM Modi Sets Target Of 6 Crore 'Lakhpati Didis' Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday set a target of making six crore women 'Lakhpati Didis', saying this would bring a major transformation in the rural economy through the strength of women. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of Red Fort on India's 80th Independence Day, Modi said the government has already surpassed its target of making three crore women 'Lakhpati Didis'. The Lakhpati Didi initiative is a flagship Indian government programme under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). It aims to empower women in Self-Help Groups to achieve a sustainable annual household income of Rs 1 lakh or more "We have surpassed the target we had set of making three crore sisters 'Lakhpati Didis'. Now, we are moving forward with the target of creating six crore Lakhpati Didis," he said. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 11:18 (IST) ### "Our children now fight for their rights": Arvind Kejriwal On Independence Day Aam Aadmi Party National Convenor, Arvind Kejriwal, on Saturday said the younger generation was increasingly raising its voice over the condition of government schools, calling the demand for basic facilities such as desks, clean drinking water, toilets and teachers a reflection of "true freedom" on Independence Day. In an Independence Day post on X, Kejriwal said this year's August 15 was "even more special" as children across the country were coming forward to demand better facilities in their schools. "This August 15th is even more special. After Gen Z, now Gen Alpha has taken up the charge. Children across every corner of the country are fighting to get their schools fixed. They are demanding basic facilities for their schools like desks, clean water, toilets, and teachers. Our children have learnt to fight for their rights. That's what true freedom is... Heartfelt Independence Day wishes to all of you." > ये 15 अगस्त और भी ज़्यादा ख़ास है, > > Gen Z के बाद अब Gen Alpha ने मोर्चा संभाल लिया है। देश के कोने-कोने में बच्चे अपने स्कूल को ठीक करवाने के लिए लड़ रहे हैं। वे अपने स्कूल के लिए desks, साफ पानी, toilets और शिक्षकों जैसी बुनियादी सुविधाओं की मांग कर रहे हैं। > > हमारे बच्चों ने… pic.twitter.com/iU9OD2ArtN > > — Arvind Kejriwal (@ArvindKejriwal) August 15, 2026 Aug 15, 2026 10:23 (IST) ### AI Training, Free Coaching: PM Modi's 6 Big Announcements On Independence Day Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday announced a series of major initiatives focused on youth development, technology, education, sports, civil defence, semiconductors and nuclear energy while addressing the nation on the 80th Independence Day from the Red Fort. The announcements included a nationwide AI skilling programme for one crore youth, free online coaching for competitive examinations, civil defence reforms, a sports talent hunt for children, expansion of semiconductor manufacturing and new targets for nuclear power generation. Aug 15, 2026 09:59 (IST) ### PM Modi Meets Schoolchildren After Independence Day Address At Red Fort Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday interacted with schoolchildren at the Red Fort after delivering his address to the nation on the occasion of India's 80th Independence Day. As soon as the Prime Minister concluded his speech, a group of schoolchildren dressed in white, green and saffron rushed towards him. Modi stopped to interact with them and shook hands with several children, creating an emotional moment at the culmination of his Independence Day address. The Prime Minister had earlier led the national Independence Day celebrations at the historic Red Fort in New Delhi. He hoisted the National Flag from the ramparts of the Red Fort and addressed the nation, outlining his vision for a 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047. This year's celebrations carried special significance as the country marked 150 years of 'Vande Mataram'. For the first time, the National Song was rendered as part of the Independence Day ceremony at the Red Fort. The Prime Minister said the occasion was historic and linked the spirit of 'Vande Mataram' with India's journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047. During his address, Modi emphasised the need for collective efforts to build a self-reliant and developed India. He said the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 represents the aspirations of more than 140 crore Indians. (ANI) Aug 15, 2026 08:59 (IST) ### PM Modi Says India Emerging As Widely Respected Nation Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said that India's influence and standing across the world have been increasing on several fronts, with the country emerging as a widely accepted and respected nation in the international community. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the iconic Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India's stable political mandate, stable government, vibrant democracy, strong judiciary and the Constitution have contributed to strengthening the country's position globally. "Today, India is emerging in the eyes of the world as a widely accepted and respected nation. India possesses a stable political mandate, a stable government, a vibrant democracy, a robust judiciary, and guiding all of us is the Constitution of India. The world has now truly begun to recognise these intrinsic strengths of ours," he said. PM Modi also highlighted the Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and trade partnerships India has finalised with several countries since 2014. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lead the 80th Independence Day Celebrations from the Red Fort. Satheesan, during the Independence Day celebrations at Central Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram on Saturday (August 15, 2026), called upon people to become “guardians and fighters of a strong democracy founded on open-mindedness, tolerance, debate, self-correction and innovation.” Remembering the flood victims, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Saturday (August 15, 2026) said the State government was preparing a comprehensive rehabilitation plan for the flood-affected families. ##### Independence Day special story: How democracy is unfolding across India This Independence Day, perhaps the most important reminder for us as citizens is that democracy is rebuilt and sustained through dialogue and interaction. When people across socio-economic and political backgrounds connect, share grief and laughter, make friends, chat and get to know one another, they begin to build something more fundamental: trust. ***Read the full story here:*** ### Independence Day 2026: How protest, community and tea are bringing people together Explore how protests, community kitchens, and shared experiences are fostering trust and connections among diverse groups in India. ##### Indians define what freedom means to them | Independence Day 2026 * August 15, 2026 23:25 Leading countries extend greetings to India on 80th Independence Day India’s global partners, including France, Russia and Australia, on Saturday (August 15, 2026) extended greetings to the country on its 80 th Independence Day, reaffirming their commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and regional cooperation. ### Leading countries extend greetings to India on 80th Independence Day World leaders, including Macron and Putin, extend heartfelt greetings to India on its 80th Independence Day, celebrating strong ties. * August 15, 2026 20:39 One shouldn't speak lies from Red Fort: Akhilesh on PM speech “Red Fort is not a place from where one should speak lies,” Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday (August 15, 2026) hit out at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his pitch for women’s reservation bill in his Independence Day speech saying the legislation was already passed in 2023 and the government should implement it in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Mr. Yadav also claimed that Partition is a cause for celebration for the BJP. In his speech from the ramparts of the Red Fort, Modi urged political parties to rise above differences to help secure 33 per cent reservation for women in legislatures. Speaking to reporters at the Samajwadi Party office here, Yadav said, “One should not speak lies from the Red Fort. It is not the place from where lies should be spoken.” *- PTI* * August 15, 2026 20:37 41 policemen honoured in Gurugram on Independence Day On the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, 41 police officers and personnel were honoured for outstanding services, officials said. Addressing a State-level event here marking the 80th Independence Day, the Chief Minister made five major announcements, including removing the maximum limit of six chances for the State civil service exam. This is not merely a matter of protocol; it is a question of the nation’s honour,” Mr. Thakur said. “Driven by petty politics and a policy of appeasement, the Congress has insulted the National Song today. The Congress must apologise to the entire nation,” he added. Mr. Thakur claimed that while the original version of ‘Vande Mataram’, which he alleged was earlier “discarded or removed” by former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, was being sung, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi appeared uncomfortable. *- ANI* * August 15, 2026 20:32 L-G Saxena joins people in celebrating 80th Independence Day in Ladakh Ladakh Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena on Saturday joined the people of the Union territory in celebrating the 80th Independence Day by hoisting the national flag at the polo ground here and taking the salute of the marching contingents. Addressing the gathering, Saxena paid tribute to the freedom fighters whose courage and sacrifice secured the country’s Independence and laid the foundation for its democratic journey, an official statement said.
