Mr. Shah’s message comes amid Nepal’s efforts to strengthen ties with India, with the Himalayan nation seeking greater economic cooperation and connectivity with its immediate neighbour. “On the occasion of India’s 80th Independence Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings and best wishes to PM @narendramodi and the friendly people and Government of India,” Shah’s office said in a post on X. *- PTI* * August 15, 2026 17:09 'Suryapath Tiranga': Global relay of tricolour spirit to mark 80th Independence Day ‘Suryapath Tiranga’ -- a first-of-its-kind initiative, involving several Indian missions, from east to west, under which the images of the tricolour is being “digitally relayed” across multiple time zones, began from India’s High Commission in Fiji on Saturday (August 15, 2026) to mark the country’s 80th Independence Day. The campaign symbolically traces the journey of the rising sun across time zones, carrying the spirit of India’s freedom, unity and national pride across continents, officials said. “With the first rays of the sun, the Indian flag was raised first in Suva, Fiji, marking the beginning of the global Tiranga relay, ‘Surya Path Tiranga’ - a symbolic journey carrying the spirit of India’s Independence Day across the world,” the High Commission of India in Fiji posted on X. *- PTI* * August 15, 2026 17:08 Governor inaugurates first organ transplant centre in Sikkim Sikkim Governor Om Prakash Mathur on Saturday (August 15, 2026) inaugurated the first organ transplantation centre and post-transplant ICU at STNM Hospital here. Two Sikkimese patients underwent kidney transplants for the first time within the State. The Governor inaugurated the facilities in the presence of Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang and Health Minister GT Dhungel. Speaking to reporters after the inauguration, Mr. Tamang called the commencement of kidney transplantation in Sikkim a “historic milestone”, saying it had been achieved on the state’s 80th Independence Day. *- PTI* * August 15, 2026 17:07 Only two decades left to achieve 'Viksit Bharat' goal, says Gujarat Dy CM; calls for planning Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi on Saturday (August 15, 2026) called for planning to achieve the ambitious goal of ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047, saying only two decades were left to meet the target. He was addressing a gathering after hoisting the national flag at the Manjalpur Sports Complex in Vadodara as part of the district-level Independence Day celebration. “Only 20 years remain until India completes 100 years of independence. Prime Minister Narendra Modi set the goal of Viksit Bharat at 2047 five years ago. There are now only two decades to achieve this ambitious goal. Therefore, the 80th Independence Day is not merely a celebration; it is a great source of inspiration for planning the next 20 years,” he said. *- PTI* * August 15, 2026 16:45 Telangana CM inaugurates statues of Nehru, Rajiv Gandhi Chief Minister of Telangana, Revanth Reddy, inaugurated the statues of former Prime Ministers Jawahar Lal Nehru and Rajiv Gandhi at Sangareddy District, Telangana. *Photo: Mohd Arif* WhatsApp Image 2026-08-15 at 4.42.12 PM.jpeg * August 15, 2026 16:01 This generation brings with it qualities that give us every reason to be confident: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant The Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant, in his Independence Day address at the Supreme Court on Saturday (August 15, 2026), said the younger generation’s “remarkable resilience”, awareness of social realities, and their use of technology to communicate and access knowledge give the nation every reason to be confident in them. ### The Bar and Bench walk with you: CJI to youth in I-Day message, a day after Bar Council overreach CJI Surya Kant praises youth's resilience and tech-savviness in Independence Day address, emphasizing their role in shaping justice. * August 15, 2026 15:56 Return what was taken away from J&K: Omar Abdullah in his I-Day speech Terming federalism as “strength of the country”, J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, said on the 80th Independence Day on Saturday (August 15, 2026) in Srinagar, that J&K should be returned “whatever was taken away from it”, in an oblique reference to the special status under Article 370. *Read more here,* * August 15, 2026 15:07 Visual story: Freedom's Progress Through the Years India’s independence was the culmination of nearly two centuries of political change, resistance, and negotiation. This timeline revisits the milestones that shaped India’s struggle for independence, as recorded by *The Hindu*. ### Freedom's Progress Through the Years Explore an interactive timeline of Indian democracy, dissent, constitutional milestones, protests, and the Emergency through archival visuals and key historical events. * August 15, 2026 15:05 Working on comprehensive rehab plan for flood-hit families: Assam CM Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Saturday (August 15, 2026) said the State government was preparing a comprehensive rehabilitation plan for the flood-affected families. He said the focus of such a plan would be on rebuilding infrastructure, restoring livelihoods, and creating a more flood-resilient Assam. In his Independence Day message, the Chief Minister emphasised stronger infrastructure, reliable early-warning forecasts, and resilient livelihoods, maintaining that a rapid digital assessment of the flood damage would enable faster rehabilitation and reconstruction. **Read more here,** * August 15, 2026 14:13 Chaos at Kozhikode Corporation’s I-Day flag-hoisting as councillors simultaneously sing national anthem, Vande Mataram The Independence Day flag-hoisting ceremony at Kozhikode Corporation in Kerala on Saturday (August 15) witnessed unusual scenes when two groups of councillors sang the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana, and the national song, Vande Mataram, simultaneously. ### Chaos at Kozhikode Corporation’s I-Day flag-hoisting as councillors simultaneously sing national anthem, Vande Mataram Kozhikode's Independence Day ceremony saw chaos as councillors sang the national anthem and Vande Mataram simultaneously, causing confusion. * August 15, 2026 14:01 Nagaland CM calls for early solution to Naga Political Issue, operationalisation of FNTA Nagaland celebrated the 80th Independence Day on Saturday (August 15) with Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio calling for unity, an early and honourable solution to the long-standing Naga Political Issue, early operationalisation of the FNTA, and continued peace and stability in the State. The state-level celebration was held at the Civil Secretariat Plaza, where Mr. Rio hoisted the National Flag, took the salute and addressed government employees and a limited gathering of the public. Mr. Rio inspected the parade and presented awards to police personnel and civil servants for meritorious and distinguished service. Students were not present at the official programme as the influential Naga Students’ Federation (NSF) enforced its boycott call against participation in it over the mandatory singing of the entire “Vande Mataram” song.- *PTI* * August 15, 2026 13:02 Nepal PM Shah greets PM Modi, Indian people on 80th Independence Day Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Saturday (August 15) extended greetings and best wishes to his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi and the people of India on the occasion of the country’s 80th Independence Day. Mr. Shah’s message comes amid Nepal’s efforts to strengthen ties with India, with the Himalayan nation seeking greater economic cooperation and connectivity with its immediate neighbour.- *PTI* * August 15, 2026 12:57 Hard work of job aspirants won't be left at mercy of paper leak mafia: Jharkhand CM Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Saturday (August 15) said the hard work of job aspirants would not be left at the mercy of the paper leak mafia, corruption or irregularities, and huge employment opportunities would be made available to them through the State’s recruitment agencies. Mr. Soren’s assurance in his Independence Day speech came at a time when agitation by students demanding reforms in Jharkhand’s recruitment examination process entered its 22nd day.- *PTI* * August 15, 2026 12:33 New system of governance central to ZPM govt's vision for self-reliant Mizoram: CM Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma on Saturday (August 15) said that a new system of governance remains central to the present ZPM government’s vision to build a self-reliant economy. Addressing the Independence Day programme, Mr. Lalduhoma said achieving self-sufficiency in food and other essential sectors was a key objective of his government, alongside improving livelihoods and ensuring balanced development across Mizoram. “We are taking steps to build a stronger system of governance and a self-reliant, more developed state, while improving the living standards of the people. To achieve self-sufficiency in food and other essential areas, our central vision has been, and will continue to be, a ‘people’s government’ with a new vision and a new approach,” he said after hoisting the Tricolour.- *PTI* * August 15, 2026 12:30 Looking back at Film and Television Institute of India's role on making India’s filmmaking rebels In the start-up years, the Institute’s annual budget was just ₹3 lakh. There were shortages galore. In fact, the teacher shortage was so dire that Jagat Murari could hardly keep the institute running. The solution? He persuaded some of the finest filmmakers to come to Pune as guest faculty. Directors such as David Lean, Satyajit Ray, Ritwik Ghatak, Raj Kapoor, Ismail Merchant, James Ivory, and many others walked through the FTII gates. Cinematographers like R.D. Mathur (of *Mughal-e-Azam* fame) and Subrata Mitra (Ray’s cameraman) came. Kamini Kaushal and Balraj Sahni taught acting. In the academic year 1963-64, he pulled in 50 such guest lecturers. **Read the story here:** ### Independence Day 2026 | Jagat Murari and FTII: Where India’s filmmaking rebels were made On India’s 80th Independence Day, the enduring legacy of Jagat Murari, FTII’s former head, asks if public institutions can still nurture independent thinkers * August 15, 2026 12:01 Mehbooba asks Centre to reflect if India has lived up to Constitution's vision PDP president Mehbooba Mufti on Saturday (August 15, 2026) called on the BJP-led government at the Centre to reflect on whether India truly embodies the principles outlined in the Constitution. “The BJP government at the Centre should think if, after 80 years, we have realised the dream of India as envisioned in the Constitution,” Ms. Mufti told reporters after attending the Independence Day function at Bakshi Stadium. Her comments came in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s request for all political parties to support the implementation of women’s reservation in Parliament and State assemblies without turning it into a political battle.- *PTI* * August 15, 2026 11:58 Country needs informed citizens, not blind followers for strong democracy, says Deputy CM K. Pawan Kalyan Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan has asked the youth to think before believing something, question before following, and inquire before taking a decision. Addressing the youth after hoisting the national flag during the 80 th Independence Day celebrations at District Police Grounds in Kakinada city on Saturday (August 15, 2026), Mr. Kalyan has reiterated, “In the era of technology, information is reaching the people at good speed, but speed is not truth. For a strong democracy, the country needs informed citizens and not blind followers”. ### Country needs informed citizens, not blind followers for strong democracy, says Deputy CM K. Pawan Kalyan Deputy CM K. Pawan Kalyan emphasizes the need for informed citizens over blind followers for a robust democracy. * August 15, 2026 11:47 Secularism, democratic consciousness and equality are our strengths and pillars: Kerala CM Addressing the State after hoisting the national flag at the Independence Day celebrations at Central Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram on Saturday (August 15, 2026), Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan called upon people to become “guardians and fighters of a strong democracy founded on open-mindedness, tolerance, debate, self-correction and innovation.” ### In Independence Day speech, Kerala CM warns against communalism, calls for open-minded democracy Kerala Chief Minister advocates for a diverse democracy, emphasizing unity, tolerance, and constitutional values in Independence Day speech. * August 15, 2026 11:43 'From Red Fort, PM claims credit for everything': Mallikarjun Kharge slams BJP on Independence Day Marking India’s 80th Independence Day at the Congress headquarters, Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge slammed the BJP-led Central government, accusing it of failing to deliver fundamental rights, evading parliamentary accountability, and fueling divisive politics while “crushing the poor.”- *ANI* WhatsApp Image 2026-08-15 at 11.17.44 AM.jpeg *Flag hoisting by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge on the occasion of 80th Independence Day at the AICC HQ, Indira Bhawan, New Delhi on Saturday, August 15, 2026. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and former president of AICC, Sonia Gandhi are also seen.* *Photo credit: Shiv Kumar Pushpakar* * August 15, 2026 11:39 Arunachal CM vows to rebuild State in better way after natural calamity ravages region Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu on Saturday (August 15, 2026) vowed to rebuild the State in a better way after floods ravaged the region, and announced a ₹7,834 crore investment between 2026 and 2029 to strengthen roads, rural connectivity and other key infrastructure. Hoisting the Tricolour at Indira Gandhi Park here, on the occasion of India’s 80th Independence Day, he said the recent natural disasters had brought back to focus the need for safer and more resilient infrastructure in the frontier State.- *PTI* * August 15, 2026 11:30 India's struggle for independence was different from the freedom struggles that had proceeded in other colonies: CJI Surya Kant Speaking during Independence Day event at the Supreme Court, CJI Surya Kant, said, “If you look back, understand that India’s struggle for independence was different from the freedom struggles that had proceeded in other colonies. Ours was not primarily an armed insurrection. It was instead a sustained challenge to the legitimacy of colonial rule through political movements, petitions, public debates and most importantly, through the language of law.”- *PTI* * August 15, 2026 11:14 Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke hoists the national flag at his native village in Maharashtra Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke hoists the national flag at his native village in Maharashtra on August 15, 2026. Mr. Dipke on said that government-run schools in India remain neglected irrespective of parties in power as he prepared to launch ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign from Hingoli in Maharashtra, marking Independence Day. * August 15, 2026 10:59 Slogans that built solidarity during freedom struggle Slogans are dispatches, a voice of persuasion and resistance, and hence, carry as much historical and cultural value as our monuments. Though the trajectory of sloganeering has evolved with time, the essence of its purpose is still the same — bringing change. ### Going viral: Slogans that built solidarity during freedom struggle Explore how powerful slogans united India’s diverse voices in the struggle for independence, shaping national identity and resistance. * August 15, 2026 10:45 Looking back: Why Chennai journalists went on a fast on Independence Day 25 years ago? On the morning of August 15, 2001, as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister J. Jayalalithaa hoisted the national flag at Fort St. George, about 3.5 km away, scores of journalists sat on a fast outside the M.A. Chidambaram Cricket Stadium, near the State Guest House in Chennai. About 48 hours earlier, several journalists, particularly photographers and camerapersons, had been subjected to a savage attack by the police just outside the office of the Director of Police on Dr. Radhakrishnan Salai. ***Read the full article here,*** * August 15, 2026 10:11 Watch: Independence Day celebrations from across the country Independence Day celebrations are under way across the country. Here are glimpses from a few States: * August 15, 2026 10:01 Modi urges all to join 100-day anti-drug campaign Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a collective effort to make India drug-free, urging families to join the 100-day nationwide Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan. In his address to the nation on the 80th Independence Day, Modi said drug addiction has emerged as a major challenge for the country’s youth, and stressed the need to tackle it. “Drug addiction is becoming a very big challenge for the country and its youth. Making India drug-free should be a collective responsibility of all of us,” he said from the ramparts of the Red Fort. “For our bright future, our youth generation should be strong, our youth should be capable and should work for the country,” he said. Mr. Modi urged volunteers, NGOs, social and cultural organisations and spiritual leaders to prepare for the 100-week campaign for a drug-free India. *-PTI* * August 15, 2026 09:54 PM Modi's I-Day speech shortest in four years Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered a 75-minute Independence Day speech on Saturday (Augst 15, the shortest in four years and his fourth shortest ever. On India’s 79th Independence Day last year, Modi had delivered a 103-minute speech, breaking his own record of a 98-minute address delivered on the 78th Independence Day in 2024. His longest Independence Day speech before 2024 was for 96 minutes in 2016, while his shortest speech was in 2017, when he spoke for 56 minutes. - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 09:37 'Dimagi Naxals' looking to create unrest, must identify, isolate them: Modi Maoist extremism is breathing its last in the country, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, as he called for “identifying and isolating” the “dimagi Naxals”. Addressing the nation on the 80th Independence Day, the Prime Minister said Naxalism and Maoism destroyed the future of several youths. “For four decades, huge areas and people were in their clutches under the fear of guns. Over 3,500 security personnel died protecting people; the number is higher than those who die in war,” he said. “When we came to power in 2014, we swore to rid the country of Naxals. I am happy Maoist violence is taking its last breath,” he said, adding that several areas have become free of Naxalites and are becoming developed. Mr. Modi added, “For years, those with Naxal mentality had their place in the power corridors. They were in government committees as advisors. Maoist thinking impacted policies. “We have succeeded in getting rid of armed Naxals in the jungles, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ are looking for opportunities to create violence, unrest … They want to drag the society on the wrong path,” he said. - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 09:17 Modi announces free online coaching for youth Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced free online coaching for aspirants preparing for competitive exams to ease the financial burden on their families. “Coaching classes burden the poor and the middle class. We will provide free online coaching for various exams,” Mr. Modi said in his address to the nation on India’s 80th Independence Day. “Every parent feels that if they do not send their child to a coaching class, they are not a prestigious family,” he said. The Prime Minister said he assures these families that they can save “thousands of crores of rupees” spent on coaching, be close to their children, and care for them. - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 09:10 Added 650 new universities, doubled medical seats, since 2014: Modi Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country added 650 new universities in the last decade and more than doubled the number of medical seats since 2014. In his address to the nation on the 80th Independence Day, Modi said the government brought in a new education policy after decades. “For 35 years, there was no education policy. We brought a new education policy,” he said from the ramparts of the Red Fort. “From 2004 to 2014, there were fewer than 350 universities. And today, within 10-12 years, nearly 650 new universities have been added,” the Prime Minister said. “Before 2014, there were only 400 medical seats, and today nearly 850 medical seats are available,” he added. - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 09:01 PM Modi appeals to all parties to support 33% reservation for women in Parliament In his speech, Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to all parties to extend their support for Women’s reservation in Parliament and Assemblies. “33% reservation for women is call of the hour, appeal to all parties to support and take credit for it,” he said. * August 15, 2026 08:46 Centre, state, industry must work together for Viksit Bharat: Modi The Centre, the state, and the industry must work together for reforms, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Saturday. In his address to the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort, Modi said that society, government, and industry must change their traditional ways, thinking, and targets to achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047. “Things that have not been done in the last five or six decades, we have to do them in the next five to seven years. I have faith in my country’s youth, farmers, labourers, daughters, and mothers to be able to do this,” he said. - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 08:36 PM Modi highlights railway electrification, green hydrogen train Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted the pace of railway electrification under his government, saying 70% of the network was electrified in 10 years compared with 30% in the previous 90 years. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, Mr. Modi said railway electrification had begun in 1925 but only 30% of the network was electrified in the next 90 years. “We completed 100% electrification in just one decade. Thirty per cent in 90 years and 70% in 10 years -- this is the pace of work,” he said. He said electrification has helped save imported diesel and benefited the environment as trains are increasingly powered by electricity. - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 08:22 Trade agreements we are signing provide big opportunity for MSMEs: PM Modi PM Modi asked MSMEs not to let go of opportunities being provided by the trade agreements being signed by the country. “World has started recognising our abilities; we have concluded FTAs with 40 countries,” he said, adding that markets of world open for Indian farmers, we have to reach there. “Our agri-products must become global brands.” “There should be no compromise with quality, our mantra should be ‘quality, quality, quality’.” * August 15, 2026 08:17 Proved naysayers wrong by ensuring sufficient energy supplies during West Asia crisis: PM Modi When West Asia crisis happened, some people tried to scare us that we will not get petrol, diesel or LPG, PM Modi says during his address, adding that his government proved naysayers wrong by ensuring sufficient energy supplies. “Some people weaponised systems at their disposal during times of crisis, but our self-reliance helped us.” “Due to our measures there is no shortage of gas, fuel, urea in country today,” he added. * August 15, 2026 08:11 India moving forward on harnessing alternative sources of energy: PM Modi PM Modi said India is moving forward on harnessing alternative sources of energy. “We have set target of 200 GW nuclear energy, setting up 5 new nuclear reactors,” he said, adding that over 50 lakh households in country now covered by solar energy. Piped gas is reaching 1.75 crore households today, he said. * August 15, 2026 08:07 PM Modi assures flood, landslide-hit families of government support Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured families affected by floods and landslides in several parts of the country that the government stands with them and shares their pain. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort after hoisting the national flag on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, Modi said, “My dear Indians, in the past few days, some parts of the country have witnessed floods and landslides, and many families have been affected. We fully understand their pain and suffering. I assure the affected families that the entire country stands with them.” He expressed solidarity with those affected by the natural calamities. - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 08:05 Energy security is the demand of our times: PM Modi Saying that Energy security is the demand of our times, PM Modi added that his Government has taken several steps for this. Mr. Modi also urged self-reliance, saying “We cannot remain dependent on other nations.” “Many countries are now depending on India for critical minerals,” he said adding that India has set up semi-conductor plants in its bid to become ‘aatmanirbhar’ * August 15, 2026 07:56 We must dream big, because big dreams expand our thinking and broaden the horizons of our vision: PM Modi Addressing the nation from ramparts of Red Fort, PM Modi, says, “A nation becomes great and achieves its aspirations when it moves forward on the strength of its dreams, its resolve and its capabilities. My fellow citizens, our country can no longer be driven by small dreams. We must dream big, because big dreams expand our thinking and broaden the horizons of our vision. Our resolve must be firm. When our resolve is strong, the ability to find a way through difficulties and disasters emerges on its own.” - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 07:51 5,000 special guests from diverse backgrounds attend 80th I-Day celebrations Nearly 5,000 special guests from different walks of life, including women entrepreneurs, young innovators, farmers and beneficiaries of various government schemes, are in attendance at the 80th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort. The invitees included International Yoga Day volunteers, women entrepreneurs under the PM Mudra Yojana, beneficiaries of schemes including NAMASTE, PM AJAY and SEED, and best performing My Bharat volunteers. Best performing beneficiaries of PMAY(U), street vendors under PM SVANidhi, urban sanitation workers under the Swachh Bharat Mission, best performing Delhi Metro workers, workers associated with Kartavya Path and Central Vista, staff of government hospitals in Delhi were also part of the gathering. The special guests also included young innovators under national innovation programmes, scientists in different fields, cab drivers of Bharat Taxi in Delhi, interns under the Prime Minister Internship Scheme, and best performing start-ups supported under various government schemes. - *PTI* * August 15, 2026 07:47 'We must realise the dream of Viksit Bharat by 2047': PM Modi During his address to the nation, PM Modi calls upon Indian citizens to realise the dream of Viksit Bharat by 2047. Mr. Modi says that despite gaining freedom in 1947, the country couldn’t gain speed towards becoming a developed country. * August 15, 2026 07:42 Watch LIVE: PM Modi addresses the nation on Independence Day * August 15, 2026 07:41 PM Modi begins address PM Modi has begun his addresses to the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort in New Delhi. Prior to the this, for the first time, the National Song, ‘Vande Mataram’, was rendered during the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort. * August 15, 2026 07:13 PM Modi pays floral tributes at Rajghat * August 15, 2026 07:03 India's constitutional values, democratic institutions have faced serious challenges: Kharge Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said India’s constitutional values, democratic institutions and social harmony have faced “serious challenges” over the last 10 years, as he called for full measure of equality and justice for the economically-weaker sections. In his message to people on India’s 80th Independence Day, Mr. Kharge said the country has travelled a long way, but many aspirations still remain unfulfilled. * August 15, 2026 07:01 PM Modi greets people on Independence Day Prime Minister Narendra Modi greeted people on the occasion of Independence Day and said powered by 140 crore Indians, the country is scaling new heights of progress across different sectors. Mr. Modi also paid tributes to the countless freedom fighters whose courage, sacrifice and unwavering commitment ensured the end of colonial rule. overview.content: ## MyGovIndia's Post --- ### **MyGovIndia** July 27 at 2:54 AM Every year on 15th August, the Prime Minister addresses the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort, outlining the vision and roadmap for India's growth. Citizens are invited to share their ideas, suggestions, and vision for #NewIndia for the upcoming Independence Day Speech 2026. Selected inputs may feature in the address to the nation. #IndependenceDay2026 All reactions: 156 comments 103 shares Like Comment Most relevant Sivaramakrishnan Mahadevan Youth are talented, bold but lack awareness. Compulsory Seva in Nation building, corruption free environment and Education which brings National pride. * 2w 4 Sanjaya Holey One area that deserves attention is the lack of contemporary, high-energy songs for our festivals, rich Indian traditions, and patriotic occasions that resonate with Gen Z and younger audiences. While we have a vast heritage of timeless music, there are relatively few modern compositions with fresh beats and production that young people can connect with and enjoy dancing to. A possible solution would be to organize a pan-India music competition inviting composers, lyricists, and performers to create original songs inspired by our cultural traditions and patriotic themes. The music could draw from indigenous and semi-classical genres while incorporating contemporary arrangements, rhythms, and production styles to give it a fresh, appealing flavor. Such an initiative would not only preserve and promote our cultural heritage but also make it more engaging and relevant for younger generations, encouraging greater participation in festivals and national celebrations. * 2w 3 Rajasekaran Lada Dear Modiji- This is an excellent idea to generate ideas from grounds up from the citizens to generate a vision and make India a developed nation. While I am a Canadian citizen of Indian origin, India is my home and I contribute to India by training Indian students to be young scientists. In my opinion: 1. All Indians must understand the history of our country and how the freedom was fought. Freedom and independence were gained through struggles with people’s lives lost. People must understand what the real meaning of freedom and independence means. It’s is not about one can do anything and get away with it. Freedom is responsibility. Independence allows people to think constantly for the betterment of humanity as a whole. 2. Understanding the meaning of development. Development in true sense is not about no of cars on the road, no. Mobile phones or materialistic. Development in true sense is the entire society raised to a level that they all have equal opportunity for education, health, employment, invent and innovate, social justice, Freedom with lowest divide between rich and poor. It is not about how many billionaires in the country but how many people are happy and how many people can walk freely in the middle of the night. Remember Gandhi’s dream- true freedom and independence is when a women or a child can walk freely without fear in the middle of the night. 3. Focus of world class education: provide equal standards of education to all. No more provincial standards, metriculation or CBSC. Make the standards sane all over India. The admissions must purely be based on merit for any educational programmes in the university and for employment. Totally restructure educational institutions. No third grade colleges or PSEs. It is not the no. Of colleges in a country that is important but how many are in the world rankings. Invest in building world class colleges and universities. Introduce Innovation and Invention as a part of their curriculum. Entrepreneurship must be a part of their programme. Once we have more and more entrepreneurs there will be more employment. Once we create an education and entrepreneurship ecosystem, there will not be any unemployment problem. 4. Eliminate corruption: corruption is a societal cancer. Corruption must be unearthed in India to be a truly developed nation. There are many dimensions to corruption. Once when all are gainfully employed, and punishment for corruption is made severe, transparency becomes a policy in everything we deal with, this can naturally be eliminated. 5.Tax: Everyone should pay tax. However small they earn, everyone should file a tax return. A country cannot be developed if only 25-30 per cent of the population pays taxes. There can be a bear minimum for exemptions but all should file tax return when it is self employed or working in an organization. 6. Build innovation clusters and ecosystem, where innovators, industries and educational institutions can all come together to provide solutions and creating a “circular economy”. Every mega city shall have an agenda or a vision to create such an innovation cluster. 7.Security and intelligence: There are so many individuals or countries who wants India to be ruined or clawed back in developed and such a challenge will continue to emerge all the time. Focus on enhancing intelligence and security measures is a top most priority. It is not just only some agency should do that every Indian should contribute to the security of the country. This could come only when every one is patriotic, watching for each other, and curbing security challenges. Rewarding and paying our military and intelligence personnel well and treating them well after their retirement. 8. Social welfare: There should be protection when people loose their jobs, something like social net. Welfare system for the deserving, employment insurance for those who are in need (the individuals must contribute to this fund while working), central retirement pension scheme (people need to contribute to this fund, while working, private or government or self employed) everyone must be protected under this scheme. 9. Health for all. Provide ambulances to rural areas up to certain population for anyone to access it. Hospitals, flying doctors, mobile hospitals would help to provide such a facility. Heath is a right and to build a healthy community and a healthy nation. There is more and I would be delighted to have a conversation and if I could be of any help I would be delighted to help. * 2w 1 Vivek Dubey Please consider below as the same aligns with the viksit Bharat vision: 1.Tech Sovereignty: Position India as a global semiconductor hub, export the India Stack, and heavily incentivize private R&D. 2. Green Transition: Achieve energy independence through green hydrogen subsidies, decentralized solar grids, and circular economy waste plants. 3. Economic Engine: Expand manufacturing via MSME PLI schemes, modernise agriculture with AgTech, and accelerate PM GatiShakti logistics. 4. Human Capital: Drive women-led development, fully implement the NEP, and upgrade Ayushman Bharat with advanced diagnostic networks. 5. Smart Cities: Build 100+ smart satellite cities via digitalisation. Use Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, AI, and fast networks to manage daily services 6. Global Footprint: Secure the 2036 Olympic bid, finalize western FTAs, and cement India as the premier global manufacturing alternative. Thanks and all the best. * 2w 2 Jyoti Verma May we always walk head held high, on the beautiful roads of the land with all the pride Where every child shares a story of Glory Bright Not one ,not two ,May every life shine in wisdom, compassion and courage Right Where every child love to Be Indian With A Greater Smile Where every Voice is heard and embraced where all are one and still shine with their uniqueness where expressions are fearless and flights have limitless skies! * 2w 2 Vrinda Borker Dear Modiji We have to focus on values from young age. We have to develop sense of belongingness and gratitude in them towards family, teachers, state and nation. 'Universal Human Values' by Prof. Rajeev Sangal component may be applied for senior students and also by modifying it for preprimary, primary school, and school students. We want the next generation to be literate, besides it should be resposible, cultured, innovative and patriotic. The focus is only on competitive exams. They should be able to handle failures. They should display their best culture, etiquettes when they are in distress and should be able to convey message correctly and make best use of freedom of speech.They should be habituated for using best vocabulary. This is possible only if equal importance is given to competitive exams, language, etiquette and values. Filthy language improper gestures are signs of uncivilized society. This thinking should be imbibed in them as a part of learning. * 2w 2 Randhir K Jha Please include in speech to encourage people about cleanliness and keeping clean society. * 2w 4 Indrasish Sen Firstly - To address youth, especially Gen Z with what the Government is thinking and doing about their future along with job opportunities in India in near future. Secondly, a road map on education for all and put a cap on cost of higher studies, even in Private Colleges. Thirdly, put a cap on medical costs of treatment at all hospitals including Private Hospitals and to restrict the prices of medicines in all categories like Cancer and so on. In this context, appreciate government's decision to open Generic Medicine shops. These stores should also cater broader spectrum of medicines. Fourthly, bring in appreciation of Citizen's involvement in building the society and India, as a whole. Fifthly, inform Indians about the massive drive that the current government has taken in keeping India safe from intruders, including space programs. Sixthly, effective and positive steps by which the government wants to bring down the prices of daily commodities like oil, pulses, rice and so on. * 2w 1 Subhajit Goswami Talk about promise abolishing reservation after Higher Secondary Exam to give priority on merits of Nation to represent India in the entire world. Talk about promise to expand Industry on PPP model for revenue generation by GOI this year. Talk about promise for employment to all citizens by this year. Talk about free health care and care for senior citizens for all * 2w 1 Madhu Gupta ROAD MAP OF DEVELOPED INDIA: What is the road map of developed India? CITIZENS CONTRIBUTION: role of each citizen in making the country developed ACCOUNTABLE GOVERNANCE for developed country STRONG EDUCATION SYSTEM CORRUPTION FREE SYSTEMS * 2w 2

overview.content: View Market Dashboard # Saptadhara to civil defence and vision for the Gen-Z: Key takeaways from PM Modi's Independence Day speech from Red Fort ## Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday greeted the nation on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, marking his 13th consecutive Independence Day address from the Red Fort. From semiconductors and energy reforms to national security and self-reliance, here are the key takeaways from his speech **Swati Gandhi** Updated15 Aug 2026, 09:18 AM IST Independence Day: PM Modi On Iran, Ukraine Wars - 'Some Spread Rumours; Those In AC Rooms Said…' Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday extended his greetings to the people on the 80th Independence Day, saying India, driven by the collective efforts of 140 crore citizens, is achieving new milestones across various sectors. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort in the national capital, PM Modi paid tribute to the countless freedom fighters whose courage, sacrifices and steadfast dedication helped bring an end to nearly 200 years of colonial rule. Extending his greetings to the people, PM Modi wrote in a post on X, “Warm greetings on the occasion of Independence Day. We remember with gratitude the countless freedom fighters whose courage, sacrifice and unwavering commitment ensured the end of colonial rule.” During his address, PM Modi outlined his vision for India’s future, touching on several key areas ranging from economic growth and national security to self-reliance and development. ## Key takeaways from PM Modi’s speech on the 80th Independence Day: Quick answers to key questions •5 QUESTIONS 1 What is Saptadhara as mentioned in PM Modi's Independence Day speech?⌵ Saptadhara refers to a collection of seven visions or 'streams of power' that PM Modi outlined for India's future, aimed at providing new momentum and heights for progress. 2 Why did PM Modi emphasize energy security in his speech?⌵ PM Modi highlighted energy security to address the need for India to harness alternative energy sources and reduce dependence on other countries in light of rising geopolitical tensions. 3 How does PM Modi propose to achieve self-reliance through the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative?⌵ Through the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative, PM Modi called for reducing dependence on foreign nations by promoting domestic capabilities, particularly in critical sectors like energy and minerals. 4 What are the key components of the Viksit Bharat vision introduced by PM Modi?⌵ The Viksit Bharat vision focuses on transforming India into a developed nation by 2047, emphasizing ambitious goals, innovation, and substantial progress across various sectors. 5 What challenges did PM Modi mention regarding the West Asia crisis during his address?⌵ PM Modi addressed the West Asia crisis by discussing India's effective response to fuel supply disruptions, emphasizing self-reliance that helped avoid shortages of gas, fuel, and urea. **1. Energy, nuclear power:** Addressing the country from the Red Fort, PM Modi highlighted the importance of energy security, adding that the government has taken several steps in this direction. PM Modi further said the country is moving forward to harness alternative sources of energy. The Prime Minister noted that India has set a target of 200 GW of nuclear energy and plans to set up five new nuclear reactors, with the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, attaining criticality this year. Parliament has also cleared the SHANTI Act, which sets a target of achieving 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047. **2. Aatmanirbhar Bharat & self-reliance:** PM Modi called for reducing dependence on other nations as he pushed for Indians to become self-reliant. He noted that every Indian is now rooting for Vocal for Local and extending support to "Swadeshi" products. PM Modi said rising geopolitical tensions had exposed the risks of relying on other countries, underscoring the need to strengthen domestic capabilities in critical sectors such as energy and minerals. **3. Semiconductors & critical minerals:** Pushing for more semiconductor plants in the country, PM Modi said India would now build more such facilities and added that in the next seven to eight years, the country would have up to eight more chip plants. The Prime Minister also noted that the country has established semiconductor plants as part of its efforts towards self-reliance. He also emphasised India’s efforts to forge more partnerships on critical minerals, with several countries now depending on India for critical minerals. **4. Viksit Bharat:** During his address, PM Modi shed light on the country's Viksit Bharat goal and said, "Our success shows resolve of Viksit Bharat in 2047 cannot remain unfulfilled." He added, "Small dreams are not sufficient anymore… we should dream big… India has a big dream to become 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047. When the world's most populous nation resolves to become developed, the world will look at us differently." For Viksit Bharat, PM Modi also laid out a seven-point reform framework, 'Sapta Dhara', aimed at accelerating India's journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047: manufacturing, agro-food production and food processing, technology and innovation, logistics, defence, green and blue economy, and soft power. **5.** **West Asia crisis:** PM Modi also addressed the West Asia crisis in his speech and highlighted India's response to the fuel supply disruption that created a panic-like situation across economies. He said, "Some people weaponised systems at their disposal during times of crisis, but our self-reliance helped us." He went on to say that the Indian government proved naysayers wrong by ensuring sufficient energy supplies during the crisis, and that due to the Central government's measures, India has not witnessed a shortage of gas, fuel, and urea. **6. MSMEs & trade:** Highlighting India's growing presence in global trade, PM Modi said the country has concluded free trade agreements (FTAs) with 40 countries, adding that the world has started to recognise India's capabilities. He further said the trade agreements being signed by New Delhi provide significant opportunities for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). PM Modi also noted that the country should remain open to global markets while ensuring that Indian products meet high-quality standards. **7. Governance, democracy & legal reforms:** India has a stable political mandate and government, along with a vibrant democracy. PM Modi highlighted India's strong judicial system and the Constitution as pillars guiding the country. He said India cannot progress in the 21st century while relying on laws from the previous century, pointing towards the need for legal reforms. **8. Youth & Census:** PM Modi called on the youth to take up leadership roles and dedicate time to the ongoing Census exercise. He appealed to youngsters to actively participate in the Census process. The Prime Minister also urged young people to provide accurate information about their families digitally to help make the Census error-free. **9. Women empowerment:** PM Modi said 33 per cent reservation for women is the need of the hour and appealed to all political parties to support the move and take credit for it. He said the government is working towards creating 6 crore 'Lakhpati Didis'. **10. Civil Defence & National Security** PM Modi announced plans to establish a vibrant network of civil defence and build a voluntary force to tackle modern challenges. He said wars are no longer fought only along borders and can also target critical sectors such as banking, infrastructure and refineries. *(with agency inputs)* ### About the Author Swati Gandhi Swati Gandhi is a digital journalist with over four years of experience, specialising in international and geopolitical issues. Her work focuses on foreign policy, global power shifts, and the political and economic forces shaping international relations, with a particular emphasis on how global developments affect India. She approaches journalism with a strong belief in context-driven reporting, aiming to break down complex global events into clear, accessible narratives for a wide readership. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in English (Honours) from the University of Delhi and a Master’s degree in Journalism and Mass Communication from Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University. Her academic training has shaped her emphasis on precision, analytical rigour, and clarity in writing. overview.title: PM Modi Independence Day 2026 Speech Highlights: Prime Minister sets 2047 target, pitches self-reliance and faster growth
overview.content: Enter search text: ##### The Economic Times daily newspaper is available online now. ### # PM Modi Independence Day 2026 Speech Highlights: Prime Minister sets 2047 target, pitches self-reliance and faster growth SECTIONS PM Modi Independence Day 2026 Speech Highlights: Prime Minister sets 2047 target, pitches self-reliance and faster growth ET OnlineLast Updated: Aug 15, 2026, 08:53:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size AbcSmall AbcMedium AbcLarge Save Print Comment Synopsis *PM Narendra Modi Independence Day 2026 Speech:* Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the nation from the Red Fort on Independence Day. He articulated a significant national aspiration to achieve a developed India by 2047. Modi highlighted India's economic progress over the past twelve years, contrasting it with earlier periods. The Prime Minister also paid tribute to freedom fighters and acknowledged recent flood-affected families. PM Modi addressing nation on 80th Independence Day Prime Minister Narendra Modi, addressing the nation from the Red Fort on India’s 80th Independence Day on Saturday, said the country has set itself a “big dream” of becoming a Viksit Bharat by the time it marks 100 years of independence in 2047. Modi said India became independent with several dreams but could not maintain the pace of development for several decades. He said the country had entered the group of the “Fragile Five” economies by 2014, but had accelerated its progress over the last twelve years. “Today, India has also seen a big dream to reach new heights: that dream is to make Viksit Bharat when India marks its 100th Independence Day,” Modi said from the ramparts of the Red Fort. "The whole country is moving forward with a new resolve. India has also dreamt big--and that is the dream of becoming a developed nation by 2047. Viksit Bharat will be realised in 2047. When we (the country) pledge to become Viksit, the world also watches us. When the world's most populous country takes the resolution to become a developed nation, it becomes an introduction of our courage, and the world is compelled to look at us with a different perspective," PM Modi said in his address to the nation on 80th Independence Day. India celebrates 80th Independence Day: Track all LIVE updates here ## ‘India became independent with a lot of dreams’ Modi said the country’s journey since Independence had not progressed at the desired pace in the early decades. ### Live Events “The country became independent with a lot of dreams but couldn't pick up pace,” he said. Referring to India’s economic position in 2014, the Prime Minister said, “By 2014, we became a part of the fragile 5.” He then contrasted that period with India’s recent economic performance, saying the country had picked up pace over the last twelve years. “But in the last 12 years we picked up pace,” Modi said. "India dreaming big to touch new heights; will make sure country becomes developed by 2047," he added. Modi also stressed the need for India to reduce its dependence on other countries and build domestic capabilities. “We cannot remain dependent on other nations, we must become self-reliant,” Modi said. He said the country’s push towards self-reliance was also reflected in the growing adoption of domestic products. “People aligning themselves with spirit of vocal for local,” Modi said. The Prime Minister also said India’s progress has strengthened the resolve to achieve the 2047 development target. “Our success shows resolve of Viksit Bharat in 2047 cannot remain unfulfilled,” Modi said. ## Modi invokes ‘Sapta Dhara’ Modi also unveiled a seven-stream framework, ‘Sapta Dhara’, which he said would provide a new current of strength to India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat. The seven streams identified by the Prime Minister are manufacturing, farming, technology, Gati Shakti, defence, the green economy and soft power. “Today, I would also like to recall that era when the nation knew, understood, and heard of India's prowess in the form of the 'Sapta Sindhu'. Now, to build a Viksit Bharat, we need a new current. Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the 'Sapta Dhara' of strength before the nation. In the coming 5 to 7 years, what could not be achieved in the last 5 to 7 decades, through the prowess and power of this Sapta Dhara, we will give the nation new heights, new momentum, and the capability to surpass new goals. Alongside this, the power and potential of our youth will be fully harnessed and integrated into nation-building...” The Prime Minister linked the seven streams with the potential of India’s youth, saying their capabilities would be integrated into nation-building. ## Critical minerals, energy and chips at core of Modi's speech Modi also called for changes to laws that he said were holding back India’s progress. “India cannot march forward in 21st century by relying on laws of previous century,” the Prime Minister said. He also highlighted India’s growing role in critical minerals, saying several countries were now relying on India. “Many countries are now depending on India for critical minerals,” Modi said. The Prime Minister also pointed to India’s semiconductor push as part of its self-reliance drive. “India has set up semi-conductor plants in its bid to become 'aatmanirbhar'; production has started already,” Modi said. He said India has already begun production at three semiconductor plants, and five to eight more plants are expected to come up in the coming years. He also said India is moving forward on harnessing alternative sources of energy. "We have set target of 200 GW nuclear energy; setting up 5 new nuclear reactors," Modi said. ## Youth at centre of Viksit Bharat push Modi said young Indians would be among the biggest beneficiaries of the country’s development journey and would also be its key driving force. He said the government would focus on giving young people skills needed for the next phase of technological change, including artificial intelligence. “My dear fellow citizens, when I speak of a Viksit Bharat, when I speak of advancing the nation at high speed—who is the greatest beneficiary of this? Who is the greatest driving force behind all these efforts? If there is a driving force, it is the youth of my country. It is the power of my nation's youth. The youth have an immense role to play in the journey toward a Viskit Bharat... Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I wish to make an announcement for the youth of the country: We have resolved that in the coming one year, we will work to provide AI skill training to 1 crore youth, so that the youth of our nation possess the capability to lead the world in the domain of AI as well,” Modi said. The Prime Minister also announced free online coaching for students preparing for competitive examinations, saying the cost of coaching had become a burden for poor and middle-class families. “Coaching classes burden on poor, middle class; we will provide free online coaching for various exams,” Modi said. ## ‘Every heart is beating with Vande Mataram’ Modi began his Independence Day address by invoking the National Song, which is completing 150 years this year. “Today, every heart is beating with the rhythm of Vande Mataram. Aaj har ghar Tiranga hai, har mann Tiranga hai,” he said. He also highlighted the significance of the song being performed at the Red Fort during this year’s Independence Day celebrations. “Today is also a historic moment for everyone present at this ceremony. For the first time since Independence, Vande Mataram is echoing at the Red Fort on August 15. As the people of India celebrate 150 years of Vande Mataram, what could be a more fitting occasion than this?” Modi said. The National Song was rendered at the Red Fort as part of the celebrations, marking the first such performance during the Independence Day ceremony since 1947. ## Modi takes aim at ‘fear’ campaigns Modi also took aim at what he described as misinformation and attempts to create fear during major crises, citing the Covid-19 pandemic and the West Asia crisis. “Misinformation was spread by some during Covid-19, they derived pleasure out of it,” Modi said. He said some people had tried to create fears about the availability of essential fuels during the West Asia crisis. “When West Asia crisis happened, some people tried to scare us that we will not get petrol, diesel or LPG,” Modi said. He said government measures ensured that India did not face shortages of essential supplies. “Due to our measures there is no shortage of gas, fuel, urea in country today,” Modi said. ## Modi pays tribute to freedom fighters From the Red Fort, Modi also paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi and those who fought for India’s freedom. “I pay my tributes to Bapu and all the freedom fighters and revolutionaries on this Independence Day,” he said. ## Assurance to flood-hit families Modi also referred to the floods that have affected parts of the country in recent days. “In the last few days, some parts of the country have witnessed floods, which have affected many people. I assure the affected families that the whole country stands by them,” he said. He assured those affected that the country would stand with them as they deal with the impact of the floods. overview.title: Independence Day: From corruption to better education, Delhi speaks up
overview.content: # Independence Day: From corruption to better education, Delhi speaks up ## Amid barricades and security checks, citizens across generations in Delhi reflect on what independence means today. Written by: Tabshir Shams *New Delhi*Updated: Aug 15, 2026 03:17 PM IST Thousands gathered to hear Prime Minister Narendra Modi address the nation from the Red Fort in New Delhi on India’s 80th Independence Day on Saturday. (Express Photo by Tashi Tobgyal) Make us preferred source on Google Whatsapp twitter Facebook Reddit 5 am. Around 19 kilometres from where Prime Minister Narendra Modi would hoist the flag on the occasion of India’s 80th Independence Day, dawn was still settling over Shaheen Bagh on Saturday. Ahmad Rafiq, 78, set off for the local masjid for fajr prayers. He held a prayer bead in his right hand and in his left, a bunch of tricolour balloons. “My granddaughter bought these from her school yesterday,” he said. “I thought I would put them up in the masjid. After all, today is a celebration day for all of us.” By sunrise, the roads to Red Fort—from Kashmiri Gate to Delhi Gate and Nishad Raj Marg to Chandni Chowk—had become rivers of people, funnelled through police barricades that had sealed the area to traffic since 4 am. Outside the four gates of Red Fort Metro station, queues poured out into the heat. Only those with a valid pass, booked through the Ministry of Defence’s Aamantran portal, were allowed through. Naveen, 22, a student at Ramjas College, discovered this the hard way. He and three friends had come to watch the celebrations in person for the first time, only to be stopped near Hanuman Mandir for a valid pass. “We thought just registering was enough,” he said, as an announcement from the gate urged the crowd to hurry. “Going to see the celebration in person must feel really good—not like watching it on video.” Past the checkpoints, there were multiple layers of security: frisking, ID checks, and scrutiny of passes. Only phones and wallets were allowed in; even coins had to be left behind. Outside the police booths lay small heaps of confiscated pens, Bluetooth earphones, caps and water bottles. #### Gen Z for institutional reform, accountability In the Harike enclosure, children from Sarvodaya Bal Vidyalaya 01, Jama Masjid, sit patiently in their white uniforms, listening to Prime Minister Narendra Modi speak. (Express Photo by Tabshir Shams) Inside Red Fort, the seating enclosures carried names drawn from India’s lakes: Bhimtal, Chilika, Pangong Tso, Pushkar—echoing the river-themed enclosures at this year’s Republic Day parade on Kartavya Path. Among the seated cadets was Anshuman, 22, in a sharply pressed NCC uniform, a red best-cadet badge glowing in the sunlight pinned to his blue blazer’s front pocket. He turned briefly to catch a glimpse of PM Modi as applause broke out for an announcement on India’s nuclear power achievements, then turned back. “Our generation did not grow up to see the enslavement of India in the hands of the British. There is nothing that connects the younger generation to the Independence struggle,” he said. “We got independence from the British in 1947. Now we have to get independence from corruption, hunger, and underdevelopment.” Story continues below this ad Speaking about the Jantar Mantar protest that led to Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation as education minister, he voiced scepticism about the wave of hyperpolitics. “The protests happened, a minister resigned—it was seen as a big achievement, but people quickly moved on after that. The same happened in Nepal, in Bangladesh, and other countries. But authoritarianism and corruption returned to these countries over time. There should be a push for institutional reform, an overhaul of the system,” he said. Anshuman wants to become a civil servant—the Army was never an option, he said, because he has dextrocardia (his heart is on the right side of his chest). A little further off, in the Harike enclosure, 49 schoolchildren from Sarvodaya Bal Vidyalaya 01, Jama Masjid, sat in white uniforms. Nine-year-old, Class 3 student Asad ducked behind a friend to escape the sun as the Prime Minister’s speech turned to critical minerals. “Bhagat Singh won us our freedom,” he said solemnly. “I will one day grow up to become like him. Science is my favourite subject now.” Near a water dispenser, where people lined up for a glass of water, Ratna Kumari, 21, a final-year BA student from Haryana whose brother serves in the Air Force, offered a sharper comment. “Politicians only tell us about their successes in their speeches,” she said. “They come asking for votes with their achievement stories. It’s high time they also spoke of what they haven’t achieved yet, what’s still pending. That’s how accountability gets fixed.” Story continues below this ad #### A farmer’s past, a daughter’s future For Prafull Mohanty, 62, a retired government servant from Dhubri, Assam, independence means “good governance”. (Express Photo by Tabshir Shams) For Basavaraj, 82, a farmer from Gulbarga in Karnataka, independence meant “good rain and a good harvest”. “I was two years old when the country gained independence. I don’t remember much. But even after 80 years, seeing these many people turn up—it fills my heart,” he said, standing near Gate No 9 in a slightly torn off-white dhoti and kurta, a Nehru cap on his head. Nearby, Neha, 26, sat with her two-year-old daughter, who clenched a fistful of her mother’s silver dupatta as the Prime Minister spoke of his seven-point roadmap for the nation. “This 80th Independence Day means a better life and future for my daughter,” Neha said. “I could only study till the 12th standard due to family obligations. But our future generations should get the best education as a right so they can live the best life.” As PM Modi’s speech ended, Prafull Mohanty, 62, a retired government servant from Dhubri, Assam, reflected on what independence meant for him. Wearing a gamosa draped over his maroon shirt, with a wide smile on his face, he said, “Independence for me means good governance.” He scanned the crowd for his son, an Army officer walking a little ahead, and softened when he spotted him. “My pension comes on time, which is good. The people getting jobs in Assam now are getting them on merit. Better infrastructure is being built there,” he said, adding that the floods in Sivasagar caused a lot of destruction. As the ceremony wound down, the morning’s urgency eased off. The crowd that had rushed in now walked out slowly, unhurried. Above old Delhi, multi-coloured kites started soaring in the sky. Outside the barricades, many waited for them to open at 10 am so they could go wherever the day would take them next. © The Indian Express Pvt Ltd Tabshir Shams Tabshir Shams covers health for The Indian Express. He holds a Master's degree in International Relations from South Asian University. Before joining The Indian Express, he interned at The Hindu from December 2025 to June 2026, where he assisted in the research and editing of a book on delimitation published by The Hindu Group Publications. During this time, he also wrote for The Hindu's Text & Context section, on subjects ranging from Pakistan's military establishment to Bangladesh's elections, and reported a Spotlight feature on a jute mill in Samastipur and its ripple effects on labour migration and the local economy. In July 2025, he interned at The Indian Express, where he wrote several explainers on international relations alongside a health report. His Master's thesis examines civil-military relations in Pakistan, with a focus on the post-2019 period. ... Their dreams continue to inspire us as we work together to build a Viksit Bharat.""Powered by 140 crore Indians, our nation is scaling new heights of progress across different sectors. May this journey keep progressing at an even greater pace in the times to come," he added.Here are the key highlights:80th Independence Day: PM Modi concludes address as Vande Mataram played againPrime Minister Narendra Modi concludes his address to the nation on 80th Independence Day. Vande Mataram played after his speech as well.80th Independence Day: 50 Indian companies in the Fortune 500PM Modi set an ambition for India to have 50 companies among the Fortune 500. He also called for Indian firms to emerge as global leaders across banking, pharma, law, consulting, accounting and technology.80th Independence Day: PM Modi calls for a drug-free IndiaPM Modi highlighted the Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan and urged families to join the campaign against drug abuse. He called for collective efforts to protect young people from the menace of drugs.80th Independence Day: PM Modi on India's First Digital CensusThe prime minister noted that India’s first Digital Census is currently underway. He urgrf families to sit together and provide accurate information. He stressed that reliable data will help the government formulate better policies.80th Independence Day: PM Modi calls 33% women's reservation 'need of the hour'33% reservation for women is call of the hour, appeal to all parties to support and take credit for it: PM Modi.80th Independence Day: PM Modi announces "Saptdhara" reforms for Viksit BharatAddressing the nation from the Red Fort, PM Modi outlined his ‘Sapt Dhara’ (seven streams of strength) vision, calling for India to harness its potential in agriculture and food processing, technology and innovation, Gati Shakti, defence, the green and blue economy, and soft power. He said the initiative, along with the energy and talent of India’s youth, would help the country achieve in the next five to seven years what could not be accomplished in the previous five to seven decades. * **Manufacturing power:** Build complete domestic end-to-end value chains, from design to components, focusing on zero-defect quality, cost, and global scale * **Agriculture and food processing:** Create integrated farm-to-export supply chains for millets, spices, and fruits while transitioning to chemical-free farming * **Technology and innovation:** Evolve from a tech market into a global innovation hub leading in AI, Quantum, Space, Robotics, DPI, and Made-in-India 6G * **Gati Shakti:** Establish high-speed, seamless multimodal logistics connecting cities, highways, rail, airports, and modern industrial sea ports * **Defence Shakti:** Achieve complete strategic self-reliance by pioneering and exporting next-gen defence technologies like drones, counter-drone systems, and hypersonics * **Green and Blue Economy:** Scale sustainable growth through Green Hydrogen, renewables, and energy storage alongside full utilization of ocean, coastal, and marine potential * **India’s soft power:** Globalize Indian culture, Yoga, Ayurveda, and tourism while establishing global leadership in gaming, VFX, animation, and the creative economy 80th Independence Day: More semiconductor plants likely to become operational in next seven-eight yearsPM Modi said India has made significant progress towards self-reliance in the semiconductor sector, with three major plants already operational and their output being exported. He added that another five to eight semiconductor plants are expected to become operational over the next seven to eight years.80th Independence Day: India to get five nuclear reactors in this decade, says PM ModiEnergy security is the demand of the time. We are moving forward with the aim of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power by 2047. We aim to start five new nuclear reactors in this decade: PM Narendra Modi80th Independence Day: PM Modi reiterates vision of a developed India by 2047PM Modi reiterated India’s ambition to become a developed nation by 2047, when the country marks 100 years of independence, and said the vision would require the collective effort and hard work of its 1.4 billion citizens.80th Independence Day: PM Modi assures flood-hit families of nation's support“Recently, parts of the country have been hit by floods and landslides. Many families have been affected, and we deeply empathise with their suffering. I assure the affected families that the government and the entire nation stand with them,” PM Modi said during his address.80th Independence Day: 5,000 guests from diverse backgrounds attend Independence Day celebrationsThe special invitees included beneficiaries of various government schemes, women entrepreneurs, volunteers, farmers, artisans, sanitation workers, students, innovators, scientists, start-up founders, interns and other top-performing citizens. Over 1,500 people from different states and Union territories, dressed in traditional attire, also attended the ceremony.80th Independence Day: PM Modi's signature turbanPM Modi Modi arrived at the Red Fort on Saturday wearing a striking red tie-and-dye turban with a long trailing end. The turban featured intricate red, green and white patterns, reflecting styles associated with Rajasthani and Gujarati traditions. overview.title: PM Modi Independence Day Speech 2026 Highlights: Major Announcements from Red Fort
overview.content: # PM Modi Independence Day Speech 2026 Highlights: Major Announcements from Red Fort By Manisha Waldia **Last Updated:** Aug 15, 2026, 10:17 IST ## PM Modi’s 80th Independence Day Red Fort Speech: Check key highlights, major policy announcements, and key takeaways from the address to the nation. PM Modi Independence Day Speech 2026 Highlights During his 80th Independence Day address to the nation, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made his speech at the landmark Red Fort, where he presented his vision of a self-reliant and developed country (Viksit Bharat@2047). As it is a remarkable occasion, the celebrations have coincided with the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram, which was recited for the first time at the Red Fort during the ceremony of this year’s Independence Day. Focusing on the theme of 'Yuva Shakti' (Youth Power) and modern economic governance, PM Modi called for overcoming past hitches in making India a center for manufacturing, technology, and soft power. Now let’s take a look at the major points, recommendations, and key moments from the PM’s 80th Independence Day speech. ## Key Highlights of PM Modi's Red Fort Speech The central theme in the speech of Prime Minister Modi was the introduction of Sapta Dhara (Seven Streams of Strength) - an integrated framework designed to speed up India’s journey to a developed economy over the coming five to seven years. The seven main pillars include: * Manufacturing and Global Supply Chain: Broadening the scope of Make in India to transform the nation into an important global hub in the area of production, design, and exports. * Agriculture and Food Processing: Increasing farmers’ incomes, enhancing local fertilizer production, and modernizing food distribution systems. * Technology and Innovation: Stimulating the growth of semiconductor manufacturing, establishing the infrastructure for AI and digital public goods. * PM Gati Shakti: Growing multimodal logistics of the new generation, developing high-speed transport systems, and the construction of large infrastructure facilities. * Raksha Shakti (Defense): Pursuing complete indigenous defence production, including technologies of supersonic speed and drone technologies. * Green and Blue Economy: Implementation of renewable energy objectives, exploration of sea sources of energy, and production of marine products. * Soft Power and Creative Economy: Boosting global wellbeing through yoga and Ayurveda, launching tourism promotion projects, and developing the entertainment segment. ## 2. Important Initiatives for Youth: AI Training and Free Coaching Highlighting the importance of Yuva Shakti, Prime Minister Modi made some ambitious announcements on education and skills development programs to equip young people for jobs of the future: * Nationwide AI Training: A government initiative to help over 10 million people learn skills related to the development of AI. * Free Online Coaching for Competitive Exams: Launch of free high-quality coaching programs in digital format to provide an equal opportunity for students across tier 2 and 3 cities and villages. * Innovative Fund of INR 1 Lakh Crore: The establishment of a fund to support the commercialization of deep technology research through startup companies and R and D networks. ### 3. Self-Reliance in Semiconductors and Clean Energy Focusing on strategic autonomy, PM Modi highlighted critical advancements in high-tech manufacturing and energy security: * Semiconductor Hub: India’s first semiconductor facilities have started commercial production, while the government plans to start 5-8 new plants in the next 7-8 years. * Nuclear Power Goal: Setting the goal of building a 100 GW nuclear power capacity by 2047 with the help of the 5 new indigenous reactors. * Energy Accessibility: PM Modi talked about the achievements made during the last ten years and noted that 700 cities now use piped natural gas and that there is currently 106 GW of solar energy capacity. ## 4. Global Business Goals and Financial Changes The Prime Minister issued a challenge to local businesses and banks to start competing at the global level. * Top 5 Global Businesses: Giving goals to Indian businesses to make sure that at least one Indian bank is in the top 5 banks in the world and that at least one Indian company is listed in the global top 5 pharmaceutical companies. * Fortune 500 Goals: Aiming for 50 Indian companies to make it to the Fortune 500 in the next 10 years. * 100% Electrified Railways: Celebrating full electrification for the complete railway network, up from 30% in the past 10 years. ## 5. Social Reforms, Sports and Women’s Rights * Modi mentioned important issues about growth, sports, and unity. * Women’s Reservation Request: Calling upon all parties to cooperate with the passing of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (33% reservation of seats for women). * Planning for the 2036 Olympic Games and Grassroots Sports: Announcing the start of a nationwide search for talented children aged 5 to 15 years to help prepare future champions for India’s bidding for the Olympic Games in 2036. * Digital Population Census and Defense Services: Motivating youth to take part in the digital census process and inviting them to join the nationwide Civil Defense Service. PM Modi's address on India's 80th Independence Day underscored a shift from incremental growth to decisive, conviction-driven structural reforms. India must prepare for challenges both domestically and internationally. A voluntary force will be established to address modern security concerns. This initiative aims to build a resilient nation ready for any eventuality. The Prime Minister emphasized preparedness for future challenges. Listen to this article in summarized format Loading... × × Subscribe to Unlock AI Briefing and Premium Content New Year Offer 24 Hours Left Subscribe Now Already a member? Sign In ### What's Included * Exclusive Stories * Daily ePaper Access * Smart Market Tools * Curated Investment Ideas * Ad-lite Experience * Subscription ANI PM Narendra Modi Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday called for a stronger network of civil defence volunteers, saying India must be prepared to deal with challenges both within the country and across its borders. Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on India’s 80th Independence Day, Modi said India needed to build a voluntary force that could respond to modern security and other challenges. “I announce today from the Red Fort that we will establish a vibrant Civil Defence network in the coming days. We will familiarize them with modern systems. What measures can be put in place to protect citizens from modern-day crises? We are going to create a massive, modern Civil Defence volunteer force capable of overcoming contemporary challenges,” Modi said. ### What is Civil Defence? India's Civil Defence Rules, 1968, framed under the Civil Defence Act, provide a framework for protecting civilians, property and infrastructure during hostile attacks and other emergencies. The framework allows the Central and state governments to take preventive, protective and control measures before, during and after an attack. Civil defence measures include protecting people and property, reducing the impact of attacks and supporting response and recovery efforts. ### Live Events MORE STORIES FOR YOU✕ « Back to recommendation stories I don't want to see these stories because They are not relevant to meThey disrupt the reading flowOthers SUBMIT The Prime minister's Civil Defence announcement adds a civilian preparedness component to his broader Independence Day focus on national security and self-reliance. Earlier in the address, he said India needed to become self-reliant in defence and move beyond being a market for global defence companies. “It is important for us to become self reliant in defence,” Modi said. “When the world is thinking about itself, India cannot remain merely a market for the world. We have to become global suppliers. We have to take leadership in hypersonic defence technologies,” he said. Meanwhile, India’s domestic defence production stood at ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY26, compared with ₹46,000 crore in 2014, according to government data. Defence exports reached ₹38,424 crore in FY26. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Friday that military projects worth more than ₹8.75 lakh crore had been approved over the last year as the government works to modernise the armed forces.
