all_items.title: Independence Day 2026 Live Updates: India strong contender for 2036 Olympics; PM announces nationwide talent hunt on I-Day  - The Times of India
all_items.content: Sign In ## TOI Today's ePaper Live Independence Day 2026 Live Updates: India strong contender for 2036 Olympics; PM announces nationwide talent hunt on I-Day * Live Events Share Comments * News * India News * Independence Day 2026 Live Updates: India strong contender for 2036 Olympics; PM announces nationwide talent hunt on I-Day Share Comments # Independence Day 2026 Live Updates: India strong contender for 2036 Olympics; PM announces nationwide talent hunt on I-Day THE TIMES OF INDIA | Aug 15, 2026, 22:32:24 IST SUMMARY Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday addressed the nation from the Red Fort on India’s 80th Independence Day. He spoke about national resilience, economic preparedness and India’s ambition to become a developed nation. PM Modi highlighted the government’s preparations over the past decade to protect citizens and farmers from global crises, including the Covid-19 pandemic and conflicts in West Asia. He said these efforts have helped India move towards its Viksit Bharat 2047 goal. PM Modi also criticised those who were spreading rumours about shortages of fuel, fertilisers, energy and other essential items. He said the government had prepared for such situations years ago, helping the country remain secure and self-reliant. Amid global uncertainty and rumours, PM Modi stressed the importance of long-term planning and protecting people from the impact of international crises. He invoked the mantra, "Nagrik Devo Bhava." Referring to fears of fuel shortages during the West Asia crisis, PM Modi said strategic reserves and planning over the past 10-12 years ensured that petrol, diesel and gas remained available. "We came out of Corona, and we saw conflicts across the world. So many people predicting the future spread so many rumours; some people are looking to keep people worried, scared. Some people like to see all that from people. West Asia's crisis came; petrol pumps will not give petrol or diesel; people will not get diesel," PM Modi said. Guided by the principle of "Nagrik Devo Bhava" (Citizen is Divine), PM Modi said the government focused on absorbing the impact of global economic shocks instead of passing the burden on to citizens. * Live Events 22:32 (IST) Aug 15 Indian Embassy in Azerbaijan celebrates 80th Independence Day with patriotic fervour The Indian Embassy in Azerbaijan celebrated the country's 80th Independence Day with great enthusiasm, with members of the Indian diaspora and Azerbaijani citizens participating in the festivities. The celebrations commenced with a rendition of 'Vande Mataram,' followed by the hoisting of the National Flag by Ambassador Abhay Kumar. The gathering then joined in singing the National Anthem. Addressing the gathering, Ambassador Kumar recalled the sacrifices of India's freedom fighters and reflected on the country's remarkable journey over eight decades. He highlighted India's emergence as a major economy, the world's largest democracy, and a leading voice of the Global South, founded on democracy, diversity, constitutional values and inclusive development. The Ambassador also read out President Droupadi Murmu's message on the occasion. Certificates were distributed to winners of the 'Bharat Ko Janiye Quiz' and participants in workshops on Madhubani, Warli, Gond and Phad painting traditions. 21:44 (IST) Aug 15 Ministry of External Affairs's office illuminated in the colours of the National Flag > — ANI (@ANI) 20:49 (IST) Aug 15 Prime Minister Narendra Modi greets the leaders and attendees at the At Home Reception at Rashtrapati Bhavan > — ANI (@ANI) Join conversation Share your thoughts in the comments Be respectful · TOI community guidelines 20:48 (IST) Aug 15 President Droupadi Murmu greets the leaders and attendees at the At Home Reception at Rashtrapati Bhavan > — ANI (@ANI) 20:11 (IST) Aug 15 PM Modi thanks Rabi Lamichhane for 80th Independence Day wishes > — narendramodi (@narendramodi) 19:00 (IST) Aug 15 Thousands gather at India Gate, Kartavya Path to celebrate 80th Independence Day The Central Vista came alive on Saturday as thousands carrying the tricolour gathered at India Gate and Kartavya Path to celebrate the country's 80th Independence Day, with families, tourists and youngsters spending the day taking photographs and enjoying the festive atmosphere. People started gathering at India Gate early in the morning, with lawns around the iconic monument dotted with families, many with children. Passersby stopped along the boulevard to click photographs and record videos. "We wanted to come here because Independence Day feels different when you are at India Gate. It is crowded, but the atmosphere is really nice," said Aman, who came with his family. Ice cream and toy vendors did brisk business, with children crowding stalls as families took breaks. The Central Secretariat metro station witnessed a heavy rush, with Khan Market and other nearby stations also seeing heavy footfall. The rush led to congestion on roads around India Gate and Kartavya Path, impacting traffic. Police personnel were deployed at key points to regulate traffic and manage pedestrians. "A large number of people gathered at India Gate on the occasion of Independence Day. We have deployed additional police personnel to ensure law and order, and smooth traffic movement," a senior police officer said. 17:57 (IST) Aug 15 Tricolour proudly flies on former Naxal stronghold Kurregutta Hills, J-K, says Shah Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the Tricolour now proudly flies on the hill of Kurregutta, once a stronghold of Naxal terror, and in Jammu and Kashmir, where hoisting it used to invite threats. "Where once guns roared, now patriotism echoes. The Tricolour waving over the red soil is a symbol of the strength, progress and self-confidence of a Naxal-free new Bastar," Shah said in an X post. The three-day Bastar Tiranga Yatra, covering nearly 600 kilometres through areas once considered Maoist strongholds, culminated on Friday with the hoisting of the national flag at Kurregutta hills in Bijapur district. Chhattisgarh Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Sharma and Forest Minister Kedar Kashyap led the motorcycle procession, joined by public representatives, locals and community leaders. Kurregutta had long been regarded as a formidable Maoist hideout on the Chhattisgarh-Telangana border. In another post on J&K, Shah said millions waved the national flag with joy and pride. "Jammu and Kashmir has charted a journey from fear to freedom under the leadership of Modi Ji. Where hoisting the Tiranga once invited threats, J-K now hosts Tiranga Yatras, with millions waving our National Flag with joy and pride," he said. 17:11 (IST) Aug 15 India launches 'Suryapath Tiranga' global relay to mark 80th Independence Day India has launched 'Suryapath Tiranga', a first-of-its-kind global digital relay of the tricolour, with 21 Indian missions from Fiji to Qatar sequentially hoisting the flag across time zones to mark the country's 80th Independence Day. The campaign began at India's High Commission in Suva, Fiji, around 1:30 am IST, with the flag raised as the first rays of the sun touched the island nation. High Commissioner Mehta read excerpts from President Droupadi Murmu's message, highlighting India's democratic values, economic growth and commitment to unity. "With the first rays of the sun, the Indian flag was raised first in Suva, Fiji, marking the beginning of the global Tiranga relay," the High Commission posted on X. The initiative, announced on August 7, symbolically traces the journey of the rising sun across time zones, carrying the spirit of India's freedom and unity across continents. Each mission, after hoisting the flag, tagged the next mission in the digital sequence. From 1:30 AM IST to 10:30 AM IST, 21 Indian Missions and Posts across countries from East to West hoisted the National Flag as part of the global relay, including Wellington, Beijing and Doha. The campaign will culminate with the Indian consulate in San Francisco, with over 50 Indian missions from Fiji to San Francisco participating in the initiative. 16:12 (IST) Aug 15 Putin hails India's 'remarkable progress' on 80th Independence Day, praises bilateral ties Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday extended greetings to President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi on India's 80th Independence Day, hailing the country's "remarkable progress" in economic, social, scientific and technological spheres. "Your country is making remarkable progress in the economic, social, scientific and technological spheres, and rightfully commands considerable authority in the international arena," Putin said in a message posted on the Russian Foreign Ministry's Telegram channel. Highlighting bilateral ties, Putin said Russia-India relations were "developing successfully in the spirit of a particularly privileged strategic partnership," with fruitful cooperation across a wide range of areas and close coordination within the UN, SCO, BRICS and other multilateral institutions. Putin expressed confidence that the two countries would continue to strengthen their partnership. "I am confident that, through our joint efforts, we will continue to comprehensively strengthen the constructive Russia-India partnership for the benefit of our friendly peoples and in the interests of enhancing international security and stability," he said. The greetings come as India and Russia are engaged in active deliberations to deepen bilateral cooperation along the Northern Sea Route, a vital Arctic maritime corridor. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said enhancing logistics linkages remains central to India's "multi-faceted cooperation" with Russia, with discussions on the route already underway. 16:07 (IST) Aug 15 PM Modi thanks President of Slovakia for his warm wishes on the occasion of Independence Day > — narendramodi (@narendramodi) 15:50 (IST) Aug 15 PM Modi thanks Prime Minister of Nepal for his best wishes on Independence Day > — narendramodi (@narendramodi) 15:49 (IST) Aug 15 PM Modi thanks President of France for his wishes on the 80th anniversary of Independence > — narendramodi (@narendramodi) 15:47 (IST) Aug 15 PM Modi thanks President of the Republic of Maldives for his Independence Day wishes > — narendramodi (@narendramodi) 14:03 (IST) Aug 15 'Once again used 'Naxalism' to deceive people...': Congress leader Manoj Pande hits at PM Modi over Red Fort remarks Congress leader Manoj Pande on Saturday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for failing to address pressing domestic issues during the 80th Independence Day address at the Red Fort. Speaking to ANI, Pande underlined that the people of the country wanted to see the 12-year report card of the Prime Minister, detailing government actions on key sectors. "He shouldn't have spoken like that. Today, the people of the country wanted to hear a 12-year report card: what you did for farmers, what you did for our youth, and what you did to address rising unemployment. The people of the country wanted to hear when there would be a check on rising inflation. But today, you once again used the name of Naxalism to deceive the people," he said. Further, Pande strongly condemned the use of force against the nation's youth. He alleged that last month, "lathis with nails" and pellet guns were deployed against young protesters. "Last month, the lathi with nails was used, and pellet guns were fired on the country's youth.AK-47s and pistols were fired, and even today, our children are struggling with life and death. Many children are suffering. What kind of talk is this? Go and ask them!" he said. The remarks follow PM Modi's call to identify and isolate "dimagi naxals" who threaten the country's progress. 13:11 (IST) Aug 15 A Viksit Bharat must also be an Aatmanirbhar Bharat: PM Modi > — narendramodi (@narendramodi) 12:59 (IST) Aug 15 PM announces 5-8 more semiconductor plants coming up in 7-8 years Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said India has already begun production at three semiconductor plants, and five to eight more plants are expected to come up in the coming years. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the historic Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, the prime minister said India's semiconductor journey reflects its growing technological self-reliance. "Three semiconductor plants have started. I have been told that exports have started from the production that has commenced there. I want to tell citizens, in the coming seven-eight years, 5 to 8 more are going to start," Modi said. The government rolled out the Semicon India Programme (Semicon 1.0), which was approved in December 2021 with an outlay of Rs 76,000 crore. It was launched to build a domestic semiconductor and display manufacturing ecosystem. Building on it, Semicon 2.0 has been approved in July, 2026, with a total outlay of Rs 1,27,500 crore. As many as 12 semiconductor projects have been approved across six states under Semicon 1.0, with investment commitments exceeding Rs 1.64 lakh crore. Of the 12 approved proposals, three companies -- Micron, Kaynes, and CG Semi -- have already started commercial production. One more company is expected to begin operations in 2026, further strengthening India's semiconductor manufacturing base. 12:42 (IST) Aug 15 Developing a secure India is our collective responsibility. Whether the challenge arises from within our borders or from beyond them, India is fully prepared for every situation. #### PM Modi 12:22 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day 2026: PM Modi announces modern civil defence force to tackle new-age security threats Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday announced plans to modernise the civil defence volunteer force, saying a system developed in response to conventional wars fought in past was no longer adequate when attacks could target refineries, banks, data centres and other critical infrastructure inside the country. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, Modi said the changing nature of warfare required India to strengthen not only its armed forces but also civilian preparedness against new-age threats. "Today, the nature of warfare is changing. There is no longer any guarantee that a war will only be fought along border frontiers," Modi said. He emphasised that threats could emerge far from the battlefield and target refineries, the banking system, data centres, factories and other critical infrastructure. "In these changing times, we have to increase the capability of our armed forces, but at the same time we must also prepare our citizens," the prime minister said. PM Modi noted that the country's existing civil defence system, built around the requirements of wars fought in an earlier era, had become outdated and would be prepared to meet contemporary challenges. 12:07 (IST) Aug 15 'Nehru did a lot, but did not possess arrogance': Kharge on Independence Day Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday invoked India's freedom struggle and the legacy of its first generation of leaders, remembering Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru while highlighting the Congress's contribution to the country's nation-building journey. Remembering Nehru's contribution to building modern India, Kharge on Independence Day said the former prime minister had laid the foundations of a democratic and secular nation and established institutions including IITs, IIMs and public sector undertakings. 11:59 (IST) Aug 15 Full ‘Vande Mataram’ played at Congress HQ as Kharge, Sonia, Rahul attend I-Day event The full Vande Mataram, was played at 80th Independence Day celebrations held at Congress headquarters today Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, CPP chairperson Sonia Gandhi and LoP Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and others were present on the occasion. 11:32 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day 2026: PM Modi outlines 'Sapta Dhara' for 'Viksit Bharat' 11:28 (IST) Aug 15 Every heart is beating with Vande Mataram's rhythm: PM Modi as National Song is rendered at Red Fort for first time since Independence The National Song 'Vande Mataram' was rendered for the first time during Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on Saturday, marking a historic moment at the venue. Calling the occasion historic, PM Modi said that after Independence, this was the first time that 'Vande Mataram' had echoed from the ramparts of the Red Fort during the August 15 celebrations. Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, "Today, every heart is beating with the rhythm of Vande Mataram. Aaj har ghar Tiranga hai, har mann Tiranga hai." "It is a historic day. After independence, this is the first time that 'Vande Mataram' has echoed from the ramparts of the Red Fort. For everyone present at this ceremony today, this is also a historic moment. For the first time since independence, 'Vande Mataram' is resounding at the Red Fort on August 15th," PM Modi said. 11:13 (IST) Aug 15 'Many forces don't want India to become Vishwaguru’: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Independence Day Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday called on people tostrengthen India's independence by making the country happy, prosperous, and secure so that the country becomes "Vishwaguru", noting that many people and forces are working against this goal. “We must make the nation happy, prosperous and secure, and ensure that it makes its rightful contribution to the world. However, many people and forces are working against this goal and creating obstacles. Without abandoning our principles, we must face these challenges and work to make India a ‘Vishwaguru’ — a guide to the world,” Bhagwat said at a gathering after hoisting the national flag at the RSS headquarters in Nagpur. 11:13 (IST) Aug 15 Best wishes to Indians across the world on Independence Day: Jaishankar > — DrSJaishankar (@DrSJaishankar) 10:54 (IST) Aug 15 Tricolour unfurls with the pride of 140 crore Indians: PM Modi > — narendramodi (@narendramodi) 10:43 (IST) Aug 15 Self-reliance will pave the way for India to become Viksit Bharat. We must become self-reliant and protect our interests. Today, every Indian is getting connected with initiatives of Make in India, Swadeshi, Vocal for Local. #### PM Modi 10:26 (IST) Aug 15 80th Independence Day: PM Modi announces nationwide sports talent hunt for 5-15 age group as India eyes 2036 Olympics Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday reiterated India's ambition to host the 2036 Olympics and announced a nationwide talent hunt to identify sporting talent among children aged five to 15 years, while addressing the nation on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day. Addressing the nation from the iconic Red Fort on Saturday, PM Modi said India's performance in sports has been improving, and the country is moving forward as a strong contender to bid for the 2036 Olympics. Highlighting the scope of the Olympic Games, the Prime Minister said there are around 40 sports and nearly 325-350 events, but India does not participate or qualify in nearly two-thirds of them. "In 2030, India is also going to host the Commonwealth Games," PM Modi said. "We have decided that the Olympics 2036 should be held in India. In the disciplines in which India does not play or qualify, India will focus on these disciplines, and we will launch a talent hunt campaign," he added. PM Modi said India needs to identify and nurture young talent in preparation for the 2036 Olympics, particularly children who are currently five, 10 or 15 years old. "We have to pay attention to our sons and daughters. Therefore, a talent hunt campaign will be conducted in every village, every city and every school to identify sporting talent among children aged five to 15," he said. 10:07 (IST) Aug 15 Shielding citizens, fueling dreams: PM Modi outlines India's resilience, vision on 80th Independence Day Addressing the nation from the iconic ramparts of the Red Fort on India's 80th Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered a firm message of national resilience, economic foresight, and ambitious growth. Highlighting a decade of strategic preparation, PM Modi emphasised how the government successfully insulated citizens and farmers from global shocks, ranging from the COVID-19 pandemic to ongoing geopolitical conflicts in West Asia, while steering the country toward its Viksit Bharat 2047 vision. PM Modi criticised those who were 'spreading rumours' about how the country will face problems over energy, fuel, fertilisers, and other such necessities, but the foresight in preparing for any such eventuality was already thought of a decade ago, and that has helped in keeping the country safe and self-reliant. In the face of rumours and global economic unpredictability, PM Modi highlighted the strength of India's long-term planning and insulation from global crises: "Nagrik Devo Bhava." Countering panic over potential fuel and supply shortages during the West Asia crisis, PM Modi assured that strategic reserves and thoughtful planning over the last 10-12 years kept petrol, diesel, and gas readily available. "We came out of Corona, and we saw conflicts across the world. So many people predicting the future spread so many rumours; some people are looking to keep people worried, scared. Some people like to see all that from people. West Asia's crisis came; petrol pumps will not give petrol or diesel; people will not get diesel," PM Modi said. 09:55 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day: PM Modi urges all to join 100-day anti-drug campaign Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday called for a collective effort to make India drug-free, urging families to join the 100-day nationwide Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan. "Drug addiction is becoming a very big challenge for the country and its youth. Making India drug-free should be a collective responsibility of all of us," he said from the ramparts of the Red Fort. "For our bright future, our youth generation should be strong, our youth should be capable and should work for the country," he said. Modi urged volunteers, NGOs, social and cultural organisations and spiritual leaders to prepare for the 100-week campaign for a drug-free India. "I want to tell every family that you too should become a part of this campaign. Join it and come forward to fulfil the dream of a drug-free India," he said. On August 2, the prime minister launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan' for the youths to stay away from substance abuse. 09:47 (IST) Aug 15 PM Modi urges MSMEs to leverage FTAs, take Indian products to global markets India's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) should seize opportunities created by the country's free trade agreements (FTAs) and ensure that Indian products, including textiles, machinery, medicines and seafood, reach global markets, said Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday, while addressing the nation on the occasion of India's 80th Independence Day. PM Modi said India's growing global standing and the FTAs signed with around 40 countries since 2014 have created a major opportunity for domestic businesses, particularly MSMEs. He called on them not to miss the opportunity and stressed the need for Indian products to meet global standards. "We have to reach the world. Everything that India produces should reach the world market," Modi said, adding that sectors such as textiles, machinery and pharmaceuticals have significant potential to expand their global footprint. He said India's textile industry, from Ludhiana in Punjab to Tirupur in Tamil Nadu, could expand its presence globally, while the country's fisheries and seafood sector could also benefit from greater export opportunities created by FTAs. PM Modi, however, said Indian businesses would have to meet global parameters and deliver products of the highest quality to compete internationally. 09:34 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day: Big announcements made by PM Modi today * AI Youth Skilling: 1 crore youth to be trained in AI over the next year via nationwide mission mode. * Free Online Coaching: Free online coaching will be provided to youth preparing for various examinations. * Civil Defence Reform: Modernised training and enhanced capabilities to address evolving security needs. * Sports Talent Hunt: Nationwide campaign targeting children aged 5–15 years across villages and cities. * Semiconductor: 7–8 new production plants to operationalise within 1–2 years. * Nuclear Energy: Target of 100 GW capacity by 2047 and 5 new reactors to be operational within 6–7 years. 09:33 (IST) Aug 15 Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi extends Independence Day greetings > — RahulGandhi (@RahulGandhi) 09:28 (IST) Aug 15 'Hathiyari Naxals gone but need to be wary of 'Dimagi Naxals': PM Modi hails Naxal-free India on Independence Day Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday hailed how the country has successfully uprooted naxalism from the country, remembering the sacrifice of thousands of martyred security personnel on the 80th Independence Day while addressing the nation on the iconic ramparts of Red Fort. In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity we had decided that we will rid the country of naxalism, and today I am happy to announce that naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing," the Prime Minister added. Recalling the historical significance of the ‘Sapta Sindhu’, PM Modi said India now needs a new current of strength to meet its ambitions. He said the seven streams could help India achieve in the next five to seven years what could not be achieved in the previous five to seven decades. Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the 'Sapta Dhara' of strength before the nation. Alongside this, the power and potential of our youth will be fully harnessed and integrated into nation-building..." The seven streams span manufacturing and quality, agriculture and food processing, technology and innovation, connectivity and infrastructure, defence, the green and blue economies, and India’s soft power. **1. Manufacturing and quality** PM Modi stressed the need to make India a global manufacturing hub while maintaining international standards. He urged entrepreneurs, manufacturers and MSMEs to use the opportunity to expand India’s presence in global markets. "When it comes to quality, there should be 'No Compromise'. Therefore, our core mantra must be: 'Quality, Quality, Quality'," he said. **2. Agriculture and food processing** The second stream of the Sapta Dhara is agriculture and food production, with a strong focus on large-scale food processing. He underlined the growing importance of artificial intelligence, quantum technology, space, robotics and data centres, saying India must build the capabilities needed to lead in these areas. **4. Gati Shakti** The fourth stream is Gati Shakti, focused on seamless connectivity and modern infrastructure. PM called for faster rail links, highways, inland waterways, airports, ports and multimodal logistics hubs. "Through Gati Shakti, we must focus on seamless, high-speed connectivity across the country. We need to connect cities via high-speed rail, build modern highways, inland waterways, advanced airports, and robust multimodal logistics systems," he said. He also called for port-led development to strengthen India's infrastructure and logistics network. **5. Raksha Shakti** The fifth stream is Raksha Shakti, or defence power. Modi stressed that India must become self-reliant in defence production and eventually emerge as a global supplier. "The importance of defence capability is paramount in every sense. My dear citizens, achieving Aatmanirbharta in defence is essential; India and the world have realised that there is no alternative. When the world looks out for itself, India cannot merely remain an arms market for other nations," he said. He said strengthening domestic defence production was essential not only for national security but also for India’s strategic autonomy. **6. Green and Blue Economy** The sixth stream focuses on the Green Economy and Blue Economy. Prime Minister highlighted renewable energy, energy storage, green manufacturing and the opportunities presented by India’s vast maritime resources. "The sixth strength of the Sapta Dhara is the Green economy. We must work in the areas of renewable energy, energy storage, green storage and manufacturing. India has an opportunity in the area of the Blue Economy. " He also pointed to the potential of these sectors to create new employment opportunities, including green jobs. **7. India’s Soft Power** The seventh and final stream is India’s soft power, which Modi described as an area with enormous potential both for India and the world. "The seventh strength of the Sapta Dhara is India's soft power. Today, Yoga has connected the world to India. Our Ayurveda, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming, digital content. The world is recognizing and looking forward to India's WAVES summit. We have more than 100 national parks. We have an opportunity to attract foreign tourists through the power of soft power." "India's soft power is truly immense. Today, Yoga has connected the entire world to India. Yoga is becoming a source of energy for humanity and a major pillar of trust in India. For a country rich with centres of faith, Ayurveda, holistic healthcare systems, and the 'Heal in India' initiative, we can showcase our strengths to the world through handicrafts, culture, films, our creative ecosystem, VFX, animation, gaming, and digital content. In the creative world, India can establish its pre-eminence," PM Modi said. Through the Sapta Dhara framework, Modi laid out a broad roadmap for India’s next phase of growth, combining manufacturing with agriculture, cutting-edge technology with modern infrastructure, defence self-reliance with green growth, and India’s cultural influence with its expanding global footprint. The overarching aim, he said, is to channel these seven streams of strength towards building a stronger, more self-reliant and developed India. 09:11 (IST) Aug 15 Independence Day 2026: PM Modi calls for big leap in defence manufacturing on Independence Day Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday pitched for making India a global hub for defence manufacturing, placing special emphasis on self-reliance in advanced capabilities such as hypersonic technology and drone systems. 09:02 (IST) Aug 15 ‘World is weaponising petrol, fertilisers, medicines, chips’: PM Modi on Independence Day From the ramparts of the Red Fort, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, "There was a time when I spoke of self-reliance, and people sitting in air-conditioned chambers would question what would happen to globalization. Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on India’s 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India has set an ambitious goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047 and that the world is watching the country’s journey. all_items.title: Transcript: PM Narendra Modi Speech at 2026 Independence Day, Red Fort
all_items.content: Read the full transcript of India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks (translated to English) at 80th Independence Day from the historic Red Fort in New Delhi, August 15, 2026. [TRANSLATED USING SARVAM AI) ## Tribute to Freedom Fighters and Vande Mataram at 150 Years PRIME MINISTER NARENDRA MODI: Fellow citizens, today we are all celebrating the 80th Independence Day. Today, the heartbeat of every heart echoes with the sound of “Vande Mataram.” Today, every home is the tricolour, every mind is the tricolour, and the country is moving forward with enthusiasm and excitement, with new resolutions. Many, many best wishes to all of you on Independence Day. Today, we remember with reverence those great sons who made the ultimate sacrifice for the freedom of the country. With their penance, sacrifice, and dedication, with the sole aim of freedom, they spent their entire lives in service of the nation. Today, I respectfully salute all the freedom fighters, including the revered Bapu, and the great revolutionaries who awakened the great tradition of sacrifice. Today, for all those present at this ceremony, it is also a historic moment — after independence, for the first time on August 15, “Vande Mataram” is echoing at the Red Fort. As we, the people of this country, celebrate 150 years of Vande Mataram, what could be a greater occasion than this? ## Solidarity with Flood-Affected Families My dear countrymen, in recent days, some parts of the country have been affected by floods and landslides. Many families have been affected. We fully understand their pain and suffering. I assure the affected families that we, and the entire country, stand with them. ## Big Dreams, Firm Resolutions My dear countrymen, any nation becomes great and achieves its goals when it moves forward on the strength of its dreams, its resolutions, and its capabilities. We cannot live with small dreams anymore. We need big dreams, because big dreams broaden our thinking and expand the horizon of our vision. Our resolutions must be firm — when a resolution is firm, the ability to find a way through difficulties emerges within us. And our resolutions must also be high, because when dreams are high and resolutions are high, the height of our capabilities also increases. The height of our efforts also increases, and only then can we realize our dreams. My dear countrymen, today India has also seen a very big dream — a dream seen with firm resolve, a dream to touch new heights. That dream is: when we mark 100 years of independence, in 2047, we will be a developed India. We have to achieve this goal through the efforts of 1.4 billion countrymen. And when the country with the largest population in the world takes a pledge to develop, it becomes a symbol of our courage in the eyes of the world. The world is forced to change its perspective towards us. ## Twelve Years of Progress Countrymen, I am not saying this lightly. In the last 12 years, crores of citizens of the country — Dalits, victims, the deprived, tribals, villagers, city dwellers, the poor, the middle class, youth, elderly, women and men, from North, South, East, and West — everyone has made every effort, with dedication, with a single resolve, to take the country to new heights. I respectfully acknowledge their efforts, and the result is this: in such a short time, 250 million countrymen have overcome poverty and emerged from it. It is the result of these countrymen’s efforts that, from being counted once among the “Fragile Five,” within 12 years we have become the fastest-growing major economy. Friends, we became independent with many dreams, but we couldn’t gain momentum, we couldn’t pick up speed. It happens, it goes on, we thought — it will happen, it will be seen. We remained lost in that. By 2014, the whole world had already placed us among the “Fragile Five.” In such times, over the last 12 years, India has gained new momentum. We are moving forward at a fast pace, and the countrymen have resolved that now it is impossible to stop the resolve and strength of 1.4 billion countrymen. Fellow countrymen, in the last 12 years, defense production has increased by almost four times. Khadi and village industries production has increased by almost five times. Electronic manufacturing has increased by almost seven times. The construction of modern railway coaches has increased by twenty-one times. Mobile phone production has increased by thirty-three times. Not only that, keeping pace with the modern era, we have also raised our flag in the world of digital innovation. Internet users have increased by almost four times. The number of patent grants has increased by four times. Digital transactions have increased by a hundred times. We have worked with the same seriousness towards the facilities of the common man. Every year, on average, tap water connections have been provided 15 times faster. Every year, gas connections have been provided at a rate 6 times faster. Every year, toilets for the poor have been built at a rate 4 times faster. Every year, houses have been provided to the poor at a rate 3 times faster. The country has also brought about many changes in governance. Thousands of compliances have been abolished. We abolished hundreds of old laws — the 21st century cannot march on the laws of the previous century. We expanded the metro for modern infrastructure. We strengthened public transport. The speed at which we worked, the scale at which we worked — this pace, this expansion, this achievement — the last decade has seen for the first time since independence. And when so many achievements are in front of us, and such a fast pace is visible, the strength of the countrymen is revealed every moment. The resolution to become a developed India in 2047 can never remain incomplete. All these figures testify that we are going to move forward. ## The Path of Self-Reliance My dear countrymen, for this, self-confidence is needed, self-respect is needed, and along with that, it is very important to have a self-reliant India. ## Semiconductors and Critical Minerals My dear countrymen, I will give you an example of semiconductors. After the country became independent, there was talk of semiconductors in the world, and talk about it here too. But we could not take any big plan for semiconductors forward. What is the situation today? In today’s digital world, in today’s technology, we understand the importance of chips — in electronic goods, in medical equipment, in transportation. Chips are essential in everything, and without them, a situation has arisen where the world could come to a standstill. That is why India has embarked on a major semiconductor plan towards becoming self-reliant. Three semiconductor plants have already started production, and I have been told that exports from there have already begun. I want to tell the countrymen that in the coming years, five to eight more semiconductor plants are going to start very soon. This is self-reliant India — it gives us the highway to move towards a developed India. My dear countrymen, a similar discussion is going on about critical minerals. The entire technology ecosystem is dependent on critical minerals, and India is also engaged in securing itself in this area. We have launched the National Critical Minerals Mission. We have announced a critical minerals corridor. Agreements are being made with many countries, and many countries around the world are now starting to trust India regarding critical minerals. ## Energy Security and Nuclear Power My dear countrymen, like semiconductors and critical minerals, the importance of energy is also increasing as we move in the direction the world is moving. It is now difficult to run a new world without energy — be it AI or data centers, we will need large amounts of electricity. Energy security is the demand of our time, and that is why we have already taken strong steps, one after the other, in that direction. A major medium of energy security is nuclear energy. We have passed the Nuclear Energy Act in Parliament and have decided on the path to move towards a new goal. By 2047, we are moving with the goal of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power. Within this decade, we are moving with the goal of starting five new nuclear reactors. This year, India has achieved a significant milestone by mastering fast breeder nuclear technology, and as a result, we have taken a major step towards becoming self-reliant in nuclear fuel. ## Unlocking Our Own Resources My dear countrymen, sometimes the country does not stop due to a lack of resources — the reason for stopping is the limitations of thinking. When thinking becomes confined within boundaries, we cannot even recognize our own potential. Today, the country has to depend on crude oil. This is due to our wrong thinking of the past. You will be surprised to know that we had declared 99% of our coastline as a “No Go Area.” We ourselves decided not to explore inside the sea. This was a poverty of thought. We decided this could not go on, and we opened up that 99% from “No Go Areas” to “Go Ahead Areas.” Now we are inclined to explore even inside the sea and are trying to find new reserves. Last year, taking an important step in the same direction, we announced “Samudra Manthan.” Recently, we have decided to allocate ₹85,000 crore for this work and speed it up. ## Expanding Alternative Energy My dear countrymen, I said that it is very important for us to put all our energy towards alternative sources as well, and India is working rapidly in this direction. Before 2014 — 12 years ago from today — only 70 cities in our country had piped gas supply. In 12 years, we have expanded this from 70 cities to 700 cities. This is speed, this is expansion. Before 2014, hardly 20-22 lakh houses had piped gas. Today, the work of providing piped gas is being done in three-and-a-quarter crore houses. Twelve years ago, the capacity of solar energy in the country was only 2 gigawatts. Today, we have achieved the target of 160 gigawatts. My dear countrymen, I would like to share another piece of information. We have focused equally on ensuring that the middle class and ordinary families in the country benefit from this. We launched the PM Surya Ghar Free Electricity Scheme, and today I am satisfied that in such a short time, we have crossed the figure of 5 million homes with solar energy, and it is progressing rapidly. As a result, the electricity bills of thousands of homes have become zero, and thousands of homes are earning by selling their surplus electricity. For this work, the government is providing ₹80,000 to each family. ## Railway Electrification and the Hydrogen Train My dear countrymen, you will be surprised to know this. The electrification of our railway system started in our country in 1925, but in the 90 years from 1925, only 30% of the railway was electrified. See our speed over those 90 years — just 30%. We have completed the remaining work within just one decade. 30% in 90 years, 70% in 10 years — this is how the work happens. Because of this, the diesel that we had to bring from outside has been saved. Our trains now run on electricity, and the environment has started to benefit. My dear countrymen, we have not stopped here. We do not want to be left behind in the world. You must have heard the news in the past few days — India has also touched this new field of fuel. The country has started its first hydrogen-powered train, and I am happy that it is the longest and most powerful such train. India has also hoisted its flag in the field of hydrogen trains in the world. ## Overcoming Global Crises Fellow citizens, for the last 10-12 years, we have been continuously working to achieve the target of 2047, proving ourselves step by step. We never thought we would have to face so many difficulties along the way. In these 12 years, we have faced numerous crises. The global pandemic like Covid had put the whole world in worry — all systems had collapsed. As we emerged from Covid, news of war-like situations started to arrive. Everywhere, from Ukraine to West Asia, there was an atmosphere of tension. And who knows how many soothsayers made announcements to scare the country, to keep the country terrified and worried. Some people find pleasure in spreading fear — “the vaccine will not be available,” “people will not survive Covid,” “nothing is going to happen.” When the West Asia crisis came, they said, “there will be no petrol at the pump, no gas, no diesel, no fertilizer” — spreading fear all over. Some people were enjoying scaring the people of India, terrifying them, drowning them in worry. But the country has seen that the well-thought-out plans of the last 10-12 years have borne fruit, and despite such a big crisis, the preparations India had made, taking the mantra of self-reliance as our refuge, took us forward step by step. We did not anticipate this crisis, but at that time, all our preparations came in handy. Today, the country has gas, petrol, and urea. We are standing on our own strength, moving forward. ## Shielding Farmers from Global Price Shocks My dear countrymen, these crises in the world have affected everyone; we are not untouched either. The price of urea has reached ₹3,000 per bag in the world market. Even today, we are not forcing the farmers of my country to bear that burden — the government is carrying that burden on its shoulders, and the urea bag that costs ₹3,000 in the world, we give to our farmers for only ₹300. Not only that, DAP has reached ₹5,000 in the world market today, but so that the farmers of my country do not face any problem, we are still working to provide DAP for ₹1,350. ## India’s Rising Global Standing My dear countrymen, there was a time when, as I was talking about self-reliance, some people sitting in air-conditioned chambers were telling us what would happen with globalization. But the world is seeing that over the last decade, it seems the world itself has stopped talking about globalization. Every country in the world has turned inward towards its own priorities. Unfortunately, in this time of crisis, some, to show their strength, have played the game of weaponizing resources — petrol, diesel, fertilizers, medicines, technology, chips, and even land are being weaponized. If we had not taken the mantra of self-reliance and walked in the right direction for these 10 years, imagine how difficult it would have been to face such challenges. Our preparations are continuously increasing. My dear countrymen, on the other hand, today India’s global profile is rising. India is becoming a recognized and respected country in the eyes of the world. India has a stable political mandate, a stable government, a vibrant democracy, a strong judicial system, and we all have India’s Constitution to guide us. The world has started to recognize our capabilities, and that is why, after 2014, we have entered Free Trade Agreements with almost 40 countries. ## Opportunities for MSMEs and Exports Look — what a big opportunity has come! These trade agreements are a very big opportunity, and that is why I would especially like to tell my MSMEs that we should not miss this opportunity. We have to reach the world — everything from India’s products should reach the world market, whether it is our textiles, our machinery, or our medicines. We should not miss this opportunity, but we must surpass global parameters. We must give the world what it needs, at competitive prices, and with quality. From Ludhiana in Punjab to Tirupur in Tamil Nadu, our textile sector can reach the world. Not only that, from Kerala to Gujarat, and from Tamil Nadu to Bengal — along our coastline, our fishermen brothers and sisters, due to these FTAs, have great potential for the export of our shrimp and seafood to the world. I would like to see us take advantage of this opportunity as we move forward. ## Building on a Strong Foundation My dear countrymen, the goal of 2047, of a developed India, stands on this strong foundation — the strength that the countrymen have shown over the last 10-12 years. A quarter of a century has passed, and the next quarter is extremely important for us. Now we cannot stop; our pace cannot stop. Our direction has been determined; we have to achieve it and sustain it. That is why we have to change our work culture, and while changing it, we also have to change our thinking. The pace of work that was not achieved in five to seven decades, we have to achieve in the coming 5-7 years. I have faith in the youth of my country, in the young people, in the mothers and sisters, in the farmers, in the laborers, that we can realize this dream. That is why we also have to accelerate the pace of reform. Reform is not a compulsion for us — reform is a conviction. Out of conviction, we have embarked on the reform express, and we are going to move towards the next level of reform in the coming days as well. Government, society, industry, producers, farmers — everyone has to reform their traditional systems, reform our thinking, reform our goals, and move forward with a definite direction. ## The Seven Streams (Sapt Dhara) of National Power Today, I would also like to remember the era when we knew, understood, and heard about India’s strength as the seven rivers. Now, to build a developed India, we need a new stream. Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the seven streams of power before the country. In the coming 5-7 years, we will give the country new heights and new momentum with the strength of these seven streams — something that has not happened in the last 5-7 decades — and we will build the strength to achieve new goals. Along with this, the strength of the country’s youth will be fully utilized in nation-building. ### 1. Manufacturing Power My dear countrymen, we have to take the manufacturing sector far ahead. Along with increasing production, we have to make small parts as well as big products. We should have a complete value chain — we need components, and we also need complete manufacturing of finished products. From design to manufacturing, India has to become a reliable center of the global supply chain. I want to emphasize three things to my brothers and sisters in the field of manufacturing: this is the opportunity of the times, and we should not let it go. We have to meet global standards in terms of cost, quality, and scale. Our factories should be competitive, our products should be user-friendly, our packaging should be attractive to the people of the world, and zero-defect, precision manufacturing should become our identity. Our identity in the global market should be based on credibility and quality — no compromise on quality. Our mantra should be quality, quality, quality. This will become our global brand value. ### 2. Agriculture and Food Production My dear countrymen, the second stream of the Sapt Dhara is agriculture and food processing. We have to move forward in this direction. The world’s markets are now open to our farmers because of our FTAs, and we are getting a very big market. We have to reach there — we have to go from the field to the export market. Whether it is our traditional food, our millets, our spices, or our fruits and flowers — is there anything we don’t have? These should become global brands. Our farmers will give strength to chemical-free farming, and demand for it in the world is going to increase further. If our agro products meet global parameters in every way, we will be able to reach the world easily. ### 3. Technology and Innovation The third stream of the Sapt Dhara is technology and innovation. Today’s era belongs to AI, quantum computing, space, robotics, and data centers. A completely new field has opened up, and emerging technology is challenging us every moment. We should not let the country become a market for the world — we have to become a hub of innovation. We have made our mark with UPI and digital public infrastructure, and we have put our strength to the test. Now we have to take India’s digital public technology to every corner of the world. We have to lead in next-generation communication technology — Made in India 6G should reach every corner. This should be our goal, and we should speed up our efforts towards it. ### 4. Gati Shakti (Momentum) The fourth stream of the Sapt Dhara is Gati Shakti. This momentum requires us to emphasize seamless, fast connectivity within the country. We need to connect cities with high-speed rail, we need modern highways, we need inland waterways, we need airports, and we need multimodal logistics. Our ports need to be more than just places to unload and operate goods — we don’t want world ships to simply anchor here; we need to move our ports towards port-led development and growth. ### 5. Defense Strength Our fifth stream is defense strength. It is important to become self-reliant in defense in every way. India has experienced it, the world has experienced it — there is no other option. While the world thinks only of itself, India cannot remain a market for the world. We must become self-reliant in defense by developing next-generation defense technology and move forward with the goal of becoming a global supplier. We need to develop drone and counter-drone systems, and we need to take leadership in hypersonic defense technologies. Cyber security is also becoming a challenge for every home today — that too is a field of defense in which we can channel the potential of our youth for the country and the world. ### 6. Green and Blue Economy Our sixth stream of the Sapt Dhara is the green economy and the blue economy, which also give birth to green jobs. We need to advance green hydrogen, renewable energy, energy storage, green mobility, and green manufacturing on a global scale. While the world keeps talking about global warming, we need to find solutions — India has embarked on a green movement with great potential. India also has a great opportunity in the blue economy. We have a very long coastline, and there are great opportunities in fisheries, coastal tourism, and ocean technology — areas in which we can move forward. ### 7. Soft Power My dear countrymen, our seventh stream is India’s soft power. Yoga has kept the whole world connected with India — it is becoming an energy for the world and a major reason for trust in India. India has centers of faith, India has Ayurveda, and through our holistic healthcare system, the “Heal in India” movement, we can carry our strength to the world. Be it handicrafts, culture, our films, or our creative world — VFX, animation, gaming, digital content — India can show its standing in the creative world. We have to develop it as a global strength. India has given great strength to the Wave Summit, the World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit, and it will introduce India’s soft power and creative world to the globe. India has vast wildlife resources — we have more than 100 national parks. There is a lot of potential, but we are falling short in attracting foreign tourists. We have a chance to attract tourists from around the world through our soft power, and we will do this work in the times ahead. The world’s sports events are also a great attraction — why not host them in India? The events economy is growing, and it is an attraction for the youth of the country. Everyone in the world wants to hold their events on the soil of India at some point. This is a great opportunity, and we need to establish systems to harness it. ## A Holistic Vision for Global Leadership Friends, the purpose of these seven powers of the Sapt Dhara is not just progress in one sector. With a holistic approach, we need to work towards surpassing the scale of the goals and ambitions we are pursuing. My dear countrymen, I want to connect the country’s power with the world. A country is not just a government — a country means every citizen is connected. We hear a lot about Fortune 500 companies. Why shouldn’t 50 of them be Indian companies? Why shouldn’t this be our goal? Today, the banking sector is flourishing — why shouldn’t India’s banks also be among the top banks in the world? India should have one of the top five banks globally. In the pharma sector, we have done a lot of work, but the demand of the time is that one or two Indian pharma companies should also resonate among the world’s top five pharma companies. There are law firms, there are rating agencies — isn’t it the demand of the time that we now aim for global leadership? We have talent, we have capability, we have a long history, and we have command over languages. We should reach the world. Why shouldn’t any of our consulting firms or accounting firms be among the top firms in the world? India’s technology companies should be at the forefront globally — this should be our goal. We should have brands that attract the world, brands that become the identity of our country and a destination for the world. We have to work in that direction. For this, I want to tell the state governments and local self-government institutions — and it is also the responsibility of the Government of India — to accelerate the pace of our reforms. We have to develop our systems in line with the goal of 2047. We cannot be guided by the policies and regulations of the past; we have to formulate policies according to the dreams of the future. I am fully confident that by working hard on this path, we will achieve the dream of a developed India. The central government, state governments, and industry all have to move forward together, continuing to bring reforms — not out of compulsion, but out of conviction, to achieve our goal. ## Empowering India’s Youth My dear countrymen, when I talk about taking the country forward at a fast pace, who is the biggest beneficiary of all these efforts? The youth of my country. The youth have a very big role in the journey of a developed India, and they are also its biggest beneficiaries. That is why we have to take the goal of a developed India forward with the youth as our top priority. Friends, a lot has happened in this direction over the last 10-12 years. Through the Startup India campaign, more than 2.5 lakh registered startups have been formed across the country. The Government of India has announced a ₹1 lakh crore Innovation Fund. I want to tell the youth of the country: come with your dreams, we will not let there be a shortage of resources. New opportunities for research emerged, and cheap digital data empowered the youth of Digital India. If there’s cheap data anywhere in the world, it’s on Indian soil. We created Skill India as a national program, opened up the space sector, created the National Drone Policy, and created the Khelo India policy. There was no education policy for 35 years — we brought in a new one, and middle-class families have benefited from it. Friends, from 2004 to 2014, there were fewer than 350 universities in our country. Today, within 10-12 years, about 650 new universities have been added, and we are reaching a figure of about 1,000. Before 2014, there were only 400 medical seats; today, there are almost 850 medical seats. Now, foreign universities are also coming to Indian soil, and our youth can get a foreign university degree right here in India. We are working to attract young minds to technology from childhood, and that is why we have handed over more than 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs to young children, to inspire innovation and technology from an early age. Our youth have opened many avenues in startups — India’s private space startups, run by youth with an average age of 28 years, launched their first satellite and rocket successfully on their very first trial. Today, there are more than 2.5 lakh registered startups. We recently held the AI Impact Summit. The expansion of AI is growing very rapidly, and from the Red Fort, I want to make an announcement for the youth of the country: we have decided that in the coming year, we will work to train 10 million youth in AI skills, so that the youth of our country have the ability to lead in the world of AI as well. ## The Rise of the Bio-Economy and Electric Vehicles My friends, the bio-economy is a new field. Before 2014, it was worth only ₹60,000 crore. Look at the wonders my country’s youth have done — when policies are right and goals are clear, they have shown their strength. The bio-economy business that was ₹60,000 crore before 2014 has reached ₹20 lakh crore today. In 2009-10, only one-and-a-half lakh electric vehicles were sold in our country. In 2025-26, 2.5 million electric vehicles have been sold. ## Aviation, Drones, and New Opportunities My dear countrymen, the aviation sector is also moving forward very fast for my youth. New airports, new routes, and new employment opportunities are being created in maintenance and overhaul work, providing a large amount of skilled manpower with work in the country. We have achieved success in making Made in India airplanes — the Made in India Defense Transport Aircraft, the C-295, has already taken its first successful flight. Drones have also done great work for the youth of this country. The Swamitva Yojana is being made successful in villages through drones. About 3.25 crore families have benefited from the Swamitva Yojana, and assets worth ₹140 lakh crore have been unlocked as a result, enabling people to get loans from banks and start their own businesses. ## Free Coaching for the Middle Class My dear countrymen, our middle-class families carry a very big burden — the competition of coaching classes. Every parent feels that if they do not send their child to a coaching class, they are failing their family. We are concerned about the thousands of crores of rupees spent by poor and middle-class families on this, and we want to save them from this burden, so that children can stay close to their families and be taken care of, without the financial strain falling on the household. That is why we have decided to provide free online coaching for various exams for the youth. We have digital public infrastructure, excellent talent, and teachers. By combining these resources, we are going to build a complete network to provide free coaching to the youth of the country. ## India’s Sporting Ambitions My dear countrymen, I have always said, let those who wish to play, play. Today, India is making its place in the world of sports. Now, India’s national anthem is played on sports podiums; India’s tricolour flag is seen waving. The TOPS scheme has achieved great success. Khelo India Games, University Games, Winter Games, Beach Games, sports infrastructure, coaching, sports medicine, and sports nutrition — India is now moving forward on all fronts related to sports. India’s performance in the world of sports is improving, and we are moving forward as a strong contender to host the Olympics in 2036. India is also going to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030. My friends, in the world of Olympic sports, there are about 40 types of games and roughly 250 to 350 competitions. You will be saddened to know, my countrymen — I challenge you, I appeal to you, I want your help — that in these 250-300 competitions, India has no presence in two-thirds of the games. We don’t qualify. We have decided that for the Olympics in 2036, which we hope to host in India, we want to focus especially on the disciplines in which India does not play or qualify today. Three-quarters of the share is waiting for us, and India will emphasize this. For this, we also want to run a talent-hunt campaign. If we need players for 2036, we need to focus on the youth of today — the sons and daughters aged 5, 10, and 15. A talent-hunt campaign will be conducted in every village, city, and school to find sporting talent in children aged 5 to 15. Once identified, they will be given special training to become good players for the country. ## A Drug-Free India My dear youth, addiction is becoming a major crisis for the country and its young people. A drug-free India should be our collective responsibility. For our bright future, our young generation should be strong, and our youth’s strength should be useful to our country. Recently, volunteers from My Bharat, NGOs, social and cultural organizations, and spiritual leaders of the country jointly decided on a 100-week program for a drug-free India. I want to tell every family to be a part of this campaign — join it, and help fulfill the dream of a drug-free India. ## Eliminating Naxalism and Intellectual Extremism My dear countrymen, it is very important to eliminate the decades-old challenges of the 21st century. Naxalism and Maoism have destroyed the future of millions of youth, snatching mothers’ sons away from them, ruining lives and shattering the dreams of every parent. This Naxalism had captured a large and populous part of India for four decades — at gunpoint, tearing apart the Constitution. In defense of the common citizens of the country, more than 3,500 of our police and security force personnel have been martyred — more than the number of soldiers who die in war. Our police personnel had to risk their lives so that the common man could be safe. This Naxalism had turned the earth into a land of blood. In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity, we vowed that we would free the country from Naxalism. Today, I am happy that Naxalite-Maoist violence, even in its last breath, no longer has the strength to survive. We are moving towards completely eradicating it. In the very areas where Naxalites used to fire bullets, where the earth used to be stained with blood, today the tricolour of development, trust, and effort is waving. But we are not underestimating this challenge — we need to be even more careful. For years, people with Maoist ideologies were ensconced in the corridors of power, even influencing policies through government committees as advisors. We have succeeded in eradicating the armed Naxalites in the forests and freeing the country from that crisis. But while the armed Naxalites are gone, the intellectual Naxalites are still looking for opportunities — searching for ways to spread violence and anarchy in society, resorting to various tactics to mislead people. These intellectual Naxalites must be identified, they must be isolated, and the country’s young generation must be connected to the mainstream of nation-building. ## Strengthening National and Civil Defense My dear countrymen, it is our responsibility to create a safe India. Whether the challenge is within the border or beyond, India is ready for every situation. Today, the nature of war is changing. War is no longer fought only at the border — infrastructure like refineries, banking systems, and data centers are being targeted, and factories are being destroyed in new forms of conflict. We had announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra last year, and work is progressing very fast. Today, our defense exports have increased by about 50 times, and our weapons are reaching nearly 100 countries. India’s prestige is steadily increasing on the global stage. In these changing times, we need to strengthen our weaponry and increase the capabilities of our military forces. But along with that, we also need to prepare our citizens. The civil defense systems that developed in our country, in line with the wars of the last century, have become outdated. That is why I am announcing from the Red Fort today that we will build a vibrant network of civil defense in the coming days, familiarizing citizens with modern systems that can protect them from modern crises. We are going to create a very large voluntary civil defense force to help overcome modern challenges. ## Celebrating the Power of Women My dear countrymen, in nation-building today, the contribution of our sisters and daughters has become a great source of inspiration for all of us. Whether it is fighter jets or civil aviation, our daughters are at the forefront. Whether it is the sports field, our daughters are ahead. Whether it is admission to STEM education, our daughters are leading. Girls have emerged, showing the ability to lead the country’s army with great pride. I recently visited a semiconductor plant in Sanand, where tribal girls from different corners of the country were working — girls from villages where they didn’t even know what a passport was. Those girls went abroad for training and came back to work in chip manufacturing, and the confidence they showed truly impressed me. Today, we had set a goal of making 3 crore sisters “Lakhpati Didis,” and we have exceeded it. Now we are moving forward with the goal of making 6 crore Lakhpati Didis — meaning a very big change is coming to the rural economy through the power of mothers. My dear countrymen, today, in Panchayats, Municipalities, and Municipal Corporations, a large number of our women are becoming public representatives, guiding the country, solving problems, and providing capable leadership. Keeping this in mind, we passed the Nari Shakti Vandan Act in Parliament. However, for one reason or another, this dream had fallen victim to the arena of politics for the past 40 years. Today, I stand before all the political parties of the country, under the shade of the tricolour flag from the ramparts of the Red Fort, and I appeal to you: come forward and honor the power of our women as soon as possible. Our mothers and sisters should get 33% representation in the Legislative Assemblies and the Lok Sabha, and contribute to shaping India’s policies. This is the demand of the time. I again urge all political parties: come forward, implement women’s reservation, and give rights to my mothers and sisters. ## Social Security and Healthcare for All My dear countrymen, the resolution of a developed India will only be fulfilled when development reaches the last person. Before 2014, only 25 crore people had social security cover. In the last decade, we have extended social security to 100 crore countrymen — a task that would have taken five to seven decades otherwise. With the Ayushman Bharat Yojana, even elderly people of 70 years are now getting free medical treatment up to ₹5 lakh. Crores of families have benefited greatly from this, and because of the Ayushman card, ₹2 lakh crore that would have been spent on medicines and operations is being saved for poor and middle-class families. ## A Call for Participation in the Census My dear countrymen, today I need your help with a task, and I am asking all of you, especially the youth, to take the lead. Just one or two hours of your time will give great strength to the country. These days, census work is going on in the country. Counting alone doesn’t achieve results with just figures — policies and plans are made from its nuances, and the country prepares its roadmap for moving forward. That is why having accurate information is very important. Sometimes the representatives who come from the government are in a hurry, and mistakes happen with spellings or details, which creates difficulties in getting the final results right. Now that technology is available, a decision has been made this time that you can fill in your own information for the census yourself, using your mobile phone. Later, an officer or representative will come to discuss it with you, but if you sit with your family and complete your registration digitally, there will be no mistakes in the details or spellings. The more accurate the information you provide, the more it will help the country move forward. I tell the youth of the country: sit with your family members, understand the entire form, first fill it out on paper, correct any mistakes, and then upload it digitally. This will save the country’s time and resources for the right work, and that is why I urge the youth of my country to actively participate in this census exercise. ## A Shared Resolve for a Developed India My dear countrymen, I have spoken of the seven vital streams from the Red Fort. These seven streams will give the country great strength to move forward with self-respect and with the ability to achieve its goals. We have to keep eradicating the mentality of slavery every moment. The dream of India that Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose saw, that Baba Saheb Ambedkar saw, that Pandit Nehru saw, that Sardar Patel, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru saw, that Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee saw, that Bhagwan Birsa Munda saw, that Jyotiba Phule saw — taking inspiration from all of them, we move forward. Come, let us reiterate this resolve: let the nation’s interest be above our own, and let duty be our identity. The time is ours, the opportunity is ours, the resolve is ours. Come, let’s turn dreams into resolutions, resolutions into capabilities, and capabilities into success. Let us make every step a step towards development. Let us join hands, mind to mind, staying connected to the goal — with one lamp, thousands of lamps will light up. Come, let us build a developed India together. With this one feeling, many, many best wishes to all of you on this auspicious festival. Say with me — “Bharat Mata Ki Jai! Bharat Mata Ki Jai! Bharat Mata Ki Jai! Vande Mataram! Vande Mataram! Vande Mataram!” Thank you very much. ### Related Posts * Transcript: Ben Shapiro Interview on PBD Podcast #842 * Transcript: Krystal Ball and Saagar Enjeti Interview on The Weekly Show * Transcript of Catherine Austin Fitts Interview on Tucker Carlson Show * Transcript: President Trump Remarks at Oval Office Vaccine Event * Transcript of Hunter Biden Interview on Tucker Carlson Show

all_items.title: 80th Independence Day Live Updates: 80th Independence Day Celebrations Mark 150 Years Of 'Vande Mataram'
all_items.content: 2 hours ago Aug 15, 2026 **80th Independence Day Live Updates:** The nation commemorated the 80th Independence Day on August 15, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi leading the celebrations at the Red Fort complex here amid patriotic fervour and multi-layer security. For the first time, the national song, 'Vande Mataram', was rendered during the celebrations at the Red Fort. An Army band played the tune of 'Vande Mataram' as the guests present on the occasion sang the national song. This was followed by the prime minister hoisting the national flag, and then the National Anthem was recited. The National Anthem rendition was synchronised with the 21-gun salute by the gunners of the 1721 Field Battery (Ceremonial), utilising the indigenous 105mm Light Field Guns. Floral decoration on the ramparts depicted the national flag at the centre, flanked by 'Vande Mataram' in Hindi. After the flag hoisting, the tricolour received a 'Rashtriya Salute'. Following this, flower petals were showered at the venue by two Mi-17 helicopters of the Indian Air Force -- one trooping the national flag and the other carrying a flag depicting 'Vande Mataram'. ## **Here Are The 80th Independence Day Celebration LIVE Updates:** Aug 15, 2026 23:31 (IST) ### Iranian President Congratulates PM Modi On Independence Day > Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian, President of the Islamic Republic of Iran, in a message to Shri Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India, congratulated him on the occasion of the 80th anniversary of the Independence of the Republic of India, describing the occasion as a valuable opportunity… pic.twitter.com/l0yQLlDjWA > > — Iran in India (@Iran\_in\_India) August 15, 2026 Aug 15, 2026 22:54 (IST) ### Far From Home, Young Indians in Paris Celebrate Independence Day Members of the Indian community organised a Tiranga celebration in Paris, drawing strong participation from the community, particularly Gen Z university students. The event was held to mark the occasion with patriotic fervour and to raise awareness against anti-India activities. Aug 15, 2026 20:30 (IST) ### Singapore President Congratulates India On Independence Day Congratulating India on its 80th Independence Day, Singapore President Tharman Shanmugaratnam said that both South Asian nations share a robust and forward-looking Comprehensive Strategic Partnership that is underpinned by close people-to-people ties. In a letter to his Indian counterpart, Draupadi Murmu, penned on August 15, President Shanmugaratnam also noted that the two countries’ cooperation is multifaceted, expanding into new areas of skills development, digitalisation, sustainability and advanced manufacturing. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 20:29 (IST) ### Indians, ‘Friends Of India’ Celebrate 80th Independence Day Across Globe From the Pacific islands and East Asia to Europe, the Gulf and the Americas, Indians and “friends of India” joined celebrations marking the country's 80th Independence Day on Saturday, as key partners including France, Russia and Australia extended greetings and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening ties with New Delhi. The celebrations unfolded across Indian missions and diaspora communities around the world, featuring flag-hoisting ceremonies, renditions of the national anthem and "Vande Mataram", cultural performances, community gatherings and a range of activities. At the centre of the global celebrations was the "Suryapath Tiranga" initiative, under which the Indian Tricolour was hoisted successively at Indian missions as the day moved across time zones, beginning in Fiji and scheduled to culminate in San Francisco. The initiative, part of the broader "Har Ghar Tiranga" campaign, sought to create a shared, continuous celebration stretching from one sunrise to the next. (PTI) Aug 15, 2026 18:35 (IST) Aug 15, 2026 16:58 (IST) ### Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah Greets Indian People On 80th Independence Day Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Saturday extended greetings and best wishes to his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi and the people of India on the occasion of the country's 80th Independence Day.
